Awesome tour visiting some of the most iconic landmarks. Our tour guide Mel was simply the best! Very knowledgable, funny and passionate while teaching us about the sites. He loves what he does and made learning so much fun! Thanks for an awesome day :)

Excellent tour of several iconic sites in southwest England. Catia was a superb guide and very knowledgeable about everything. Rafael was a great driver. I only wish we had more time, particularly in Bath. I can't wait to return!

Had an excellent three site tour with Peter the guide and Leston the driver. Took us to Windsor Castle, Stone Henge and Bath.
It is a highly recommended tour to experience these renowned sites. I highly recommend these company! Cheers!

Had a blast on this tour with Andy Jackson as our guide and Mark as our driver. Andy is so knowledgeable and passionate about everything tour related and then some! Mark was prompt and smooth the entire trip and got us everywhere quickly. I would definitely recommend this tour!

Richard our tour guide was very nice and knowledgeable. Michael Angelo our driver was lovely, the bus was clean and confortable, and the tour was fantastic. Very well organized, and incredibly easy for ya to navigate. I had a wonderful day

Loved Stonehenge and Windsor. Bath is a nice little place not so thrilled with the Roman baths. I know they are long drives but wish we had more time at Windsor. Security was a long wait. Our guide Katia was wonderful, she knows her history! Very good! The driver Roddy? I dont know if that was his name for sure! Was great also! Would have been nice to have bottles of water iced down we could have purchased! Lovely day! I would recommend to anyone!

This is an amazing tour and Simon is a perfect guide. He was helpful and explained everything in detail. Bath is probably worth staying for a couple of days. Windsor Castle is also a huge fun and we way the change of guards

We had a great day with our tour guide Peter and driver John. We learned a lot from Peter’s narration along the way. Loved the portable headsets so everyone could always hear when walking around. It’s the perfect way to get a taste of each of the 3 locations. Highly recommend!
Great trip, great information given by Claudia and superb driving by Mark. Plus no rain! Great opportunity to see the workings of a castle. Bath is beautiful. Stonhedge was very interesting.

This is an excellent day trip! Peter our guide was excellent! Bath and Windsor Castle (and the Windsor village) were far better than I expected and I wish we had more time in both. Stonehenge was also great but one time there will be plenty. Very well done!

Recommended if you dont have a lot of time to explore England. Fast highlights..
Windson castle visit is a bit short on time if you want to see everything. You dont really have the time to appreciatie it. Thr rest is o.k.

We could not have a better Guide than Richard. His heart and soul is dedicated to each and everyone of us enjoying this excursion! Highly recommend to All. Perfect Day of Amazing Sights outside of London. Don’t miss out on this one!

This was an awesome trip. Your guide Lalie and driver Dave - were amazing and full of knowledge. There is so much to see and do at each site. I only marked a 4 instead of 5 - as just would like more time at the locations. Maybe reduce to just two sites and split them up.
So amazing.

3 sites in one trip! Great value and get to get our to London for the day. We did get into bath late, but bath is pretty slow. Stone hedge is just how the pictures look. They are not a spectacular site, they are rocked about the early humans which I think is interesting. Windsor was closed the day I went, but still very cool to see!

Our tour guide Deborah and driver were both super friendly and knowledgeable. They made the trip very comfortable and joyful. We had so much fun. Definitely recommend. It is an awesome way to see three great historical places plus amazing countryside with great tour guides. Thank you!

The Roman Baths were fascinating. I wish we had more time here. Stonehenge was a bit disappointing. Everyone hears about it. There are some bigger and older stone placements. If I had to do it again, I'd pass on Stonehenge and double the amount of time in Bath.

Godfrey our guide and driver Sam did a fantastic job on our tour to Windsor Castle, Stonehenge, and Bath. All three sites were fun to see and the commentary was very informative and fun. Definitely recommend!

There is nothing to see. Just lot of glamour and stories only made around a useless bunch of stones. Waste of time and money. useless when compared to ancient things elsewhere like Rome, Venice or even in Paris. Funny thing is its not allowed tourist to reach the stones.

A long day in the saddle visiting Windsor Castle, Stonehenge and Bath together with Catia and the safe driving from Errol. The tour is extremely good and we learned a lot from the amazing guiding from Catia which was probably the best we have had during our trips around the globe. So very recommended from us to do this tour.

Please make note that the trip does not include any snacks or food. You will also have barely any time left to eat during each visit. Make sure to bring your own snacks, especially if you are traveling with kids.

Tour was great. Made a bit of a long day! Bruce was informative well versed in the history and how it applied. He was also very generous with additional information places to eat, places to shop a bit, and even ways to view other attractions. Would certainly do it again!
However; the directions for 1 Bulleid Way were not sufficient. They were not easily followed or adequately marked . The fact we were not returned to the same location as departure could have been troublesome for some.

This tour was very well run with an excellent, and well informed guide. The only downside for me was the brevity of the stops; however, if you only have one day and want to see all three places that is an inevitable trade off. Highly recommend!

Went with a friend and really enjoyed the day with tour guide Godfrey and the smooth driver Barry. Godfrey gave us clear instructions. Individually asked if we knew our way back and helped us with it. Thank you

Monica (our guide, and Portuguese speaker) and Paul (our driver) were splendid. The tour was spectacular, and we had the best weather you could hope for.
I deducted one star for the following: the description of the coach as "luxury". There is barely room to move. If you drop something on the floor, forget it, because there is no room to bend down to get it. No rest facilities on the coach. "Free" wifi is not free, because you have to sign in and provide contact info. The seat belts are stiff and uncomfortable. It was NOT a comfortable place to spend the hours of driving.
If I had it to do over, I would have spent one full day at Stonehenge and done the other places another time. There just wasn't enough time to really enjoy the place for me. Others may feel differently.
Windsor Castle and Bath were just right, though.
Things to know: there is no rest room on the bus. There is no USB charger on the bus. You cannot bring hot food or drink onto the bus. Most important: the bus leaves from Victoria Coach Station. This is NOT the same as the underground or train station. Leave sufficient time to find it! And drink your coffee before you get on!
PS I do not speak Portuguese. But if you do, Monica is your guide.

I have been on several day trips and tours around Europe. I often take the time to write a review and do my best to say something positive about the tour. Unfortunately, our tour guide was the absolute worst (I believe his name was Nigal), so much in fact that I can't remember anything good to say.

Our tour guide started out the trip by explaining the overall plan and explained to us that we had a very busy day ahead and it was the utmost importance that we do our best to be back to the bus on time. He even sounded like he was bragging when he informed us that just last week, he knowingly left behind a couple because they were late getting back to the bus.

Well, just so happened that I made a friend with the person I was forced to sit next to. She was a wonderful person with whom I had an instant connection. She and I paired up for the visit at the Windsor Palace. As we were heading back to the bus I stopped for the bathroom and she stopped for food. I made my way back to the bus ON TIME to the minute! I realized that she was not sitting in her seat and was immediately concerned that she had not made it back to the bus. I told Nigal she was on her way and that she likely had to use the bathroom. He became very irate stating that she better hurry or he would leave her behind. After 5 minutes past the hour, he was going to leave and I begged him to give her more time. I informed him that she was alone. He asked if she was my family and I said no. He told me that unless she was my family it shouldn't be my concern. After an exchange of words and him pubically berating me, he made it very clear that he was going to leave ONLY 8 minutes past the hour! I was furious that he would knowingly leave behind a single 20 something year old female from a country half way around the world, because she was 8 MINUTES late! Thankfully everyone made it back in the nick of time before this angry, old jerk was getting ready to pull out (there were two other people that barely made it back).

At that point I was enraged with this guy and could no longer enjoy the remainder of my day.

He also pubically berated a couple for talking while he was trying to give information about the upcoming Stonehenge. This was while we were on the bus! Seriously!?! He treated us all with disrespect. He acted like an angry, burnt out teacher forced to take kids on a field trip. He actually yelled at one lady who was trying to walk beside him to ask questions and told her to stay behind him. It was the way he addressed her that was so disrespectful.

I honestly believe this guy should be fired from the company because I will always associate Evan Evans Tours with the worst day trip I have ever taken.

Perhaps he was stressed because there was simply too much to do in one day. I felt extremely rushed throughout the day. I don't recommend this company or this tour.

Visiting these historic places definitely leaves you awestruck and inspired. Please visit!

This review focuses on the tour organisation itself and NOT the attractions.

SUMMARY:
In the end, the benefit of this trip with this company is the savings on TRANSPORTATION if you have to go alone by public transport. Otherwise, single tickets into each attraction are very affordable and you would have enough time to enjoy each attraction. Plus you won’t have to join the group queues that extend for hours. And (incase you are wondering), You do not get any express entry because you are with a company. It’s quite the opposite.

DETAILS:
I had paid for a tour to Stonehenge and Bath, but when I got to the station they told me my tour had been cancelled!! Please note that I was given no prior information about this. They then went ahead and ‘upgraded’ me to this tour. I initially wanted to visit two places so I could have enough time to soak up the history, but I had to join this because this was the only time I had as I was on a holiday.
Anyway, one thing you aren’t told is that the tour guide does NOT accompany you into any of the attractions. The tour guide simply talks on the bus and gives you instructions on when to get back to the bus. At the castle, stone henge and bath, you are really an individual trying to soak up history with a set time you must leave. Another thing they don’t mention is the queues!! For example, You will be told at the bus to “get back in 2hrs”. This seems decent. But you won’t be told that it takes an hour to queue. This leaves you with only an hour to view whatever attraction. In my case, We queued at Windsor for about an hour so we had about an hour to view the castle, the cathedral and then race back to the bus. Remember the guide doesn’t go with you into the attraction. Even worse at stone henge! There were buses taking visitors from the car park to the Stonehenge site. Hence, there were queues to get onto a bus in both directions. Both queues took me about an hour. Leaving only about 20 minutes at Stonehenge. Lastly, since many of the tourists are non English speakers, you would do well to travel with a group of friends else you may be stuck sitting with someone who speaks no English on the bus. That can be boring, especially if they are in a group themselves. Lastly, hold some change. When you are done with the tour, in the bus the guide makes a pitch for you to ‘show appreciation if you enjoyed the tour’. It’s awkward walking past his/her basket, whilst others throw in cash (the foreigners usually have cash). Never mind if you don’t care.
In all, this is good if you are only interested in pictures. I sometimes wondered how people got back to the bus so quickly! Did they even look around? :)
Good luck!

Ok, I will save majority of my comments to till the end. But let’s do some simple calculation, which unfortunately for me, no one really mentioned this before.
The travel time from Victoria station to Windsor Castle is about an hour to an hour and a half. We set off at 9am, and reach Windsor at 1030am. Change of guards happens at 11am, which last about 30min, by 12pm we had to re gather at the car park to have enough time to get to Stonehenge. ( walking time from car park to Windsor castle is between 5-7min)

Ok, so how much time we have left to walk around Windsor Castle? Do a tour on the Tower of London. For those who hasn’t, it starts at 9am and ends at 430pm. Realize the difference ?

So after departing from Windsor Castle we immediately headed to Stonehenge. Departed at 12pm and reached about 120pm, we had to be back the the carpark at 3pm for the bus heading to The Bath. 1 hour 40min sounds a good time for Stonehenge? 8 majors spots for your guided tour, taking pictures, absorbing the surrounding. I leave that to you.

Leaving Stonehenge at 3pm, we arrived into Bath at 4pm and were told that we had to leave at 530pm back to London. After alighting from the bus and walking to the Roman bath, we had to queue while the tour leader sorted out our admission tickets. By the time all was settled, time was 425pm. Hmm.. and be remindful the Bath isn’t just about the Roman Baths, itself is a beautiful small town which was worth exploring.

Now that you know the timings etc. Lets go into the group facts. We had a highly intellectual tour leader who could speak English, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese, abit of French as well she mentioned. We were a full bus load of 50 pax, and the tour was both in English and Spanish. Feeling my thoughts so far? Picture this, put in a tape recorder, press play and just listen. One way communication, everything was thrown in a one way communication.

The three places were beautiful with so much history. To really see and understand these places, would an hour plus be good enough? Well unless your goal is purely to land, snap, upload on Instagram or Facebook, and say I have been there.
I strongly discourage a 3 places with an hour drive at least from each place. Sorry to say, but the organizer of this tour seems more interested in earning the money rather then letting you really feeling the place you visited. Such route should not even be planned in the first place. $188 x 50 =$9000. Good business by providing a bus that fetch 50 pax, provide admission tickets and play a tape recorder over and over.
Btw, no offense to those who mentioned it was extremely and delightful. I was just wondering, did you guys run through Windsor Castle , and the make a sprint around Stonehenge and Bath? Just curious..

It's interesting but I don't understand what all the hype is about Stonehenge. I used to cycle there, hop over the fence and climb on the stones. I think that Avebury, 23 miles up the road is superior to Stonehenge. There are a lot more standing stones there, they spread over a larger land area and you don't have to pay to see them. You can walk round them and touch them, and you won't get struck by lightning from Zeus if you do! There's a proper museum there as well.
Stonehenge has just been taken over by an excellent marketing team to make a pile of money. There are also neolithic underground burial chambers that are interesting at West Kennet Longbarrow on the A4 west of Marlborough that are free to go inside. Why charge for viewing these historic monuments?

Booked this so I did not have to deal with the transportation. The sites were wonderful. The problem with the tour is you are trying to cover too much ground in one day. Should have researched this better. Spent more time on the bus. There was never enough time at any place to enjoy. ALWAYS rushed.

This was one of the worst experience regarding my last vacation.The company, Evan Evans driver Kevin was very unprofessional and rude, so be aware.It felt like he was targeting the only brown family.
Here, everything was rush-rush. Bring your own lunch -- there's not enough time to buy one. They expect you to eat on the bus, but no hot liquids and foods. Ok so throws fish and chips away because that’s their rule.
Our tour did not start off so well -- When we arrived to Windsor, there was a very long queue line for group tour admittance; we waited here, outside in the elements for approximately 45 minutes, without prior notice by our guide.It started to rain as soon as we got off the bus, and we stood in the rain for the next 45 minutes, getting soaked.Golden Tours offered their group members ponchos. It is the responsibility of the tour guide to alert you there is a long standing period, to which you are exposed to the elements, in a place that commonly rains. Furthermore, after 15 minutes standing in the rain, I attempted to go back to the bus to obtain our things -- the Evans bus driver was gone, while every other bus driver was in place on their coach.
That being said, you spend very little time at each location. By the time the tour guide gathers your tickets and you get into the attraction, you have about an hour at each place which is really not enough. If the company was able to pre buy and distribute tickets to passengers, this process would be greatly improved.

Evans does not provide any food, unlike Golden Tours, so also remember to get yourself food in between the very long drives otherwise you'll starve.

Me,my husband and my senior citizen parents recommend Golden Tours instead.

We booked a full day tour with evan Evan's for Windsor Castle,Bath and Stonehenge. Our tour guide Ildie ( hope this is the correct spelling of her name )
Was the worst tour guide I've ever had .
She lacked knowledge of the places we were visiting, was disjointed when trying to tell us about these places. Ildie made it a point to tell us that we had very limited time at each location ,however she did not say that the wait times getting into Windsor Castle and the Roman Baths were long. Our entry tkts did not give us a time of entry. Therefore we had to wait on ques outside and left very little time to explore each location .
She also left 2 fellow passengers behind at Windsor Castle because they did not meet her return to the bus deadline. Obe of these passengers had mobility issues. Her comment was that they should have given themselves more time to get back to the bus on time. WORSE TOUR EVER...WORSE GUIDE EVER....WILL NEVER BOOK WITH EVAN EVANS AGAIN......

Booked this from Trafalgar Square Visitor office, lovely staff! Made my way to Victoria to join. Great guide and received a lot of knowledge. My only complaint that it is quite expensive including entry fees. But, you get to see the roman baths and Stonehenge so you cant really complain.

This was one of the worst experience regarding vacation/booking/planning. The company, Evan Evan representative are very unprofessional and rude, so be aware. First , the meeting point is extremely difficult to find, not that they bother to make it anyway easy for you. Second they mentioned in very fine print that you should be there 15 min before but they leave before the 8 am and the gates to the bus close before the departure time. The representatives are rude and unprofessional with very abrasive and argumentative attitude.
My story: took forever to actually figure out where the meeting point is, there are a million of buses and companies on the pick up street. I made it couple min before 8 but happy that I made it, I stood in front of the departing bus ( with door open at that time). When I told the representative that i am in that trip she asked me to show tickets - nothing particular wrong, although they have lists of names they dont use. Be aware viator doesnt save tickets on the phone, just the link. When I asked for a minute to log on the internet, they ask me to check with the gate representative, then they closed the door and they left. The gate representative found my name is less than 10s. No one there doubted that I supposed to be in this trip despite that I actually didnt show a ticket, .... but 10s later, it was way too late. And off course it is all my fault.....I was late (although I was not), I supposed to be there 30min before!!!!!, I didnt print the ticket, although mobile tickets allowed, I should have taken a picture of the ticket on my phone etc etc. I dont think, they ever do realize that they suppose to be in hospitality business and help their costumers...
I called viator custom service which off course did nothing about it, except sending an email back. I felt very very wronged ( and 250$ waste).
I would avoid using tripadvisor as booking site for the future. Needless to say, stay away from booking stuff in London, especially with this particular company.

This tour started of promising.

It's true that you only have a short amount of time at each location.
Windsor Castle was great - make sure you pick up some food because you really won't have time to eat or pick up anything after Windsor.

Bath was fascinating & touring the old bath was such a treat however, we had to do it quickly so by the time I came out - we really only had 10 minutes left to get back to the bus.

The biggest disappointment was Stonehenge. Once we got there, it took FOREVER for the shuttle bus to pick us up! Most of the time was spent waiting for the shuttle.
When we actually got to the site, we only had 15 minutes to walk around!! I couldn't even do the audio tour they gave us. Waiting for the shuttle on the way back down was also a HUGE time suck.

If you want to get immersed in the sights - this tour is not for you. You are only briefly taking a look at these places and then moving on as a half the time, you are driving to the locations.

I probably wouldn't do this tour again.

Evans Evans did a great job with time. If my memory is correct, you’ll be at Windsor and Bath for 1.5 hours and Stonehenge one hour. Windsor felt a little rushed, but the other two were perfect. If you sit in the front of the bus, you’ll get off a little quicker and have more time at the site.

GUIDE: They won’t give tours at the sites themselves. But, before you arrive, she gave background information on the site and helpful advice (e.g. Don’t drink the water at Bath)..

BUS: It was about 1 hour to Windsor; 1.5 hours to Stonehenge, 1.5 hours to Bath. 3 hours back to London. Bring a book or some other distraction. The countryside is nice, but the three-hour ride back to London will be in the dark if you travel during the winter.

EATING: You won’t have time to eat at a sit down restaurant. Instead, your food will be grab-and-go. You may bring food and drinks on the bus, but they can’t be hot. Bring some snacks and bottled water.

UNKNOWN: Your fellow passengers can make or break a tour. We had about 40 people on our bus. Everyone in our group was on time (or if they weren’t, Evans Evans left them behind). No kids were on the tour.

We hopped on a tour bus, which was hectic to find (almost missed the bus), navigated out of London while passing iconic statues, parks, buildings, etc. to visit our first stop, Windsor Castle. The city surrounding Windsor was absolutely breathtaking, quaint and adorable. A town I could live in and never get tired of. The tour within the castle was exciting and interesting due to the history of its medieval rulers. We saw such unique beauty here and awed at the legacy of this "home".

Next we hopped back on the bus and headed out to the second stop of the trip, City of Bath. I wasn't particularly interested in this stop as I was about the first, but I instantly felt the opposite as we approached this ancient wondrous city. Founded by the Romans 2000 years ago, you quite feel the lingering vibes due to the style of architecture and the attraction we were there to see, the Roman baths. I was taken back by the state of which the Baths were preserved and how intricate the museum created the tour through it. Once we finished the tour we stopped in at a small cafe and enjoyed the remaining 15 minutes gazing at the town we were in while awaiting the bus to take us to our final destination.

On our way to Stonehenge, rolling through gorgeous countryside, we have a rather hysterical situation going on in our bus.

[TOTAL SIDE NOTE] The 4 Spanish women wouldn't stop harassing the tour guide about not translating the tour on the bus microphone instead of the headsets we were all given. The tour guide herself was Spanish, as am I, but the 35 other passengers paid for an English speaking guided tour. As a generous gesture, the company we purchased the tickets through offered to have to the guide translate everything into Spanish for them, but through the headsets. The most entertaining part of the bus riding happened when one of the ladies (seemingly having enough) stood up and started screaming "discriminacion" at the poor tour guide, until the bus driver slammed on his brakes, pulled the bus over and pretty much told her to STFU. My fiancé and I were just like what the hell is going on. We couldn't believe the women yelling and making a huge deal about this. It took myself and other Spanish speaking passengers to tell them this is an English speaking tour and it was a courtesy of the tour company to pair them with a Spanish speaking tour guide to provide commentary through headsets. Over 90% of the passengers did not speak Spanish and didn't pay to listen to Spanish commentary. I believe the tour guide, bus driver and tour company were in the right here.

Anyways, onto Stonehenge we went. This was the most anticipated site I awaited throughout my entire travels in England. Leading up to the last 3 minutes of the bus ride I was filled with butterflies. This was something I always dreamed of witnessing with my own eyes. We finally made it and I was speechless for awhile. I got chills thinking about this mysterious place that was said to have been built over 5000 years ago. we didn't get to stay long, but we cherished our time there as long as we had. Some people may say its overrated, but it was miraculous to me.

Back on the bus we headed back to London. Again beautiful scenery the whole way back. Got into the city around 9pm. I am ashamed to admit due to my dismissal of grabbing British Pound at the airport (rip off), we couldn't tip our tour guide. We got in that morning around 1am from LAX and I figured we could find a currency place before the tour that morning. Needless to say, didn't find one. She was so GREAT and I apologized for only having USD on me. She just asked for an honest review since we commented on how much we enjoyed the tour and her commentary. This is the longest review I have ever written, but it was one of the most interesting tours I have ever been on!

We opted to take this tour because we didn't have a car and wanted to see these sights. To be fair the guide said at the beginning this is just an overview to help us determine what we might like to come back and visit in depth later. I don't know if we'll ever have the opportunity to come back. Our guide was quite informative and knowledgeable but we felt incredibly rushed all day. We were given 2 1/2 hours for the Windsor Castle stop. By the time we got through the long queue and security check we had a few minutes to quickly look in Windsor Abbey then had only 40 minutes to walk through the state rooms in the castle. It was NOT enough. Stonehenge was the highlight of the day and we felt we had enough time there. And Bath, although interesting, had way too much to offer (both the baths and the town) in the time allotted. Lines for food and toilets were long all day. Suggestion: Rent a car and visit these sights on your own time.

Mel and Valentine were an excellent tour guide team. They got us to the sites quickly, often before other busses, so we'd have the most time to explore and enjoy each cite. We also magically had amazing weather that came and went while our group was off the bus. I can't say that they were blessed by G-d, but I can't say that they weren't, either.

Our tour with this company was really well put together. This highlight of the tour was our guide Mel Adams. Time is money, and Mel did everything he could to make sure our group was always of the game. We were practically first in line at the three stops which really saves you time in the end. Not to mention the guy is a historical genius, he’s a professor for crying out loud! If you can get Mel on this tour you will be lucky. He even pointed us in the direction of the best fish and chips in London.

We thoroughly enjoyed this tour. It's a great way to visit and learn about 3 beautiful places in 1 day. Our guide Mel and driver Kee were amazing. Mel is an exceptionally knowledgeable historian, who made the trip educational and entertaining. Highly recommended!

We recently spent three weeks in Europe. Our family took a bunch of tours because they typically are a good way to experience new sites and the history surrounding them. This tour was terrible - by far the worst we had. We spent more time on the bus than we did at all of the sites combined. Our tour guide tried hard (a little too hard), but she was outmatched by the number of tourists on the tour. So she pretty much yelled at us all day as they were not equipped with headsets of any kind. We spent half our time at Windsor Castle waiting in line. The lunch was miserable. They literally served us a cucumber and cheese sandwich box lunch. But hey the chips were first class. We did see three sites that would be hard to pull off in one day without a tour like this one but you’d be better to save the money and buy a train ticket, a hotel in Bath and buy your own lunch. I’m a positive guy but this tour was straight up booty cheeks.
A good trip, a good experience.Good guide. Τhe history meets the unique nature. Imposing place. Very nice.

Brief version: Would not recommend this tour company as their customer service and desire to look after their clients seems to be non existent. We booked this tour after carefully reading all the reviews on Tripadvisor but when we arrived to the Victoria Station we were blown away by the volume of travelers as well very disappointing attitude from some (not all) staff of the Evan Evans tour company. There were a number of buses leaving for this tour that morning, huge queue of people was divided into groups to board their allocated buses. When my husband and I got onto the bus we found that the only seats that were left were one all the way at the back in the middle and one in the aisle half way through the bus. When we asked our tour guide if we can board another bus so we could seat together he was very dismissive, asked if we have tried to rearrange people so we could seat together and then added, well you will be spending time at the sites together anyway (note, travel to Bath is 3 hours, one would want to travel with their travel companion, wouldn't they). Tour guide was very unaccommodating and made us fill like we are being unreasonable, at no time did he make any attempt to assist us.

We ended up deciding to not proceed with the tour and when we asked for a refund we were advised that no refunds were given. At the same time one of the staff offered another tour instead for us (Bath and Stonington only) which we ended up joining.

Second tour was more pleasant and we were given enough time at each site. We also only had 30 people on the bus so everyone was comfortable. All other buses were packed to their max.

Tips. Bring snacks, cold lunch and water with you. No hot food and drinks allowed on the bus. There is no toilet on the bus so be aware but they do make stops if requested.

We only had 3 1/2 days to see London, and this tour was the best of all! Our bus was roomy and comfortable, and our tour guide, Phil, was just amazing! He is the epitome of what you want in a guide; he's informative, interesting and entertaining. His knowledge of the local customs, pop culture, local and world history goes far beyond what is required, and that extra knowledge empowered us all. He simply loves what he does and he gives it his all. The tour was well timed and they even got us to Windsor Castle early so we could go in as soon as the gates opened. The fact that they provide headphones and an audio so we could hear everything he said form 150' away was also a great perk. Other tours were lined up behind us to get in and their guides had to yell so the group could hear the info, so our tour was definitely better. We had about 1 1/2 hours at the castle, but because we were at the beginning of the line to get in, it was enough. We saw the Changing of the Guard which was impressive. Although you aren't allowed to take pictures inside the Chapel, we saw where Meghan Markle married Price Harry and saw both her wedding dress and the military uniform he wore at the wedding. The tour of the Roman city of Bath was also beautiful and the town itself is charming and has tons of shops and restaurants to explore. Stonehenge was very interesting and 1 hour and 15 minutes was plenty of time. I give Evans Tours and especially Phil the highest rating!!! Be sure to take out some cash for a tip which the guide and driver share. I gave 20 pounds which I think is sufficient. Thank you Phil and Evans Tours for the trip of a lifetime!

This is a long day - you start before 8 and get back to London after 8 pm. Lots of time in the bus - but the sights you are going to see are all a few hours outside of London. First, Windsor Castle. This is very cool - lots to see and there is also a little "hamlet" of shops and restaurants. We only had 2 hours at this stop, so you can't see everything - best to pick either the state rooms or the chapel. We walked it all, but it was very brisk. Next stop is Stonehenge - this is a unique stop that affects everyone differently. Enough time to spend at this stop - it ends with a huge gift shop and overpriced cafe. Final stop is Bath. It was the last stop (longest away) and we had plenty of time to see everything. We also grabbed a bite to eat in the town (really cute) before the 3/5 hour trip back. Tips: If you only buy the first two sites, you will still go to all three, but not have entry fee covered for Bath (be aware). You are on your own for food, drinks (no hot food or drinks allowed on the bus) and bathroom breaks. Walking is easy, but there is a lot of it. There are stairs that may be challenging for some people - most sites are accessible, but not all.

Took the long day tour starting with Windsor, then Stonehenge, and finally Bath. Our driver Mo and Mel were great! Mel was funny, knowledgeable, and entertaining. Mo navigated the roads like a champ. However, the trip was very rushed. No fault of Mo or Mel. At the beginning of the tour, Mel forewarned us that each stop would be brief. We did not have a lot of time to explore each site and read the history. Thankfully everyone on our tour kept the time constraints and was back to the meeting place on time. Probably should only do 2 stops per tour and not 3.
Only 4 stars because......
(1) no bathroom on bus
(2) more driving then sightseeing
(3) no time to really sit and eat a meal and do the tour(s).
(4) felt rushed

We took the tour to Windsor/Bath/Stonehenge & were happy until we got to Stonehenge. We waited in line at the coach park such a long time to get a shuttle bus to the actual Stones that we had to rush around Stonehenge, almost jogging, in order to get around in time! In fact I clearly saw many people giving up on the que line and were walking to the stones instead. We couldn't walk there as we didn't know how far it was and couldn't take a chance on missing our tour bus. The Evan Evans tour guide saw us back so far in the shuttle que and asked why we were not with the rest of the group. We told him that some of the people in our little group of friends had to go to the toilet, (after being on the bus for so long, this was a necessity - this was actually the last of the three venues we toured.) He said the buses came every few minutes. He didn't offer to move us up to the rest of the group and at the time, we didn't think anything of it. Well that is apparently *not* the case! We waited a long time! While we were still waiting to get on the bus to the stones, I complained to a couple of employees at the coach park that it was taking too long. They said that it was because of all the tour buses! Well, we were told that the tour buses must make an appointment at each stop so the venue knows how many buses there will be, so logically, they knew how many people would be there! Therefore, they must know how many tour buses to expect and how many tourists will need shuttle rides! Don't blame it on the tour buses! That is just an insult to my intelligence. Had the venue kept their buses running every few minutes as promised we would have had plenty of time. After all, how long does it take for the shuttle bus to go 1.5 miles??? Certainly not 30 minutes! Then the Evan Evans tour guide said that if we wanted more time at Stonehenge, we should have taken a different tour! I was shocked! Flabbergasted! Don't blame me for choosing the wrong tour company! I believe the Evan Evans guide should have acted as our advocate! That's what we paid for, an expert with ties to the area to guide us smoothly through the venues. We paid good money for something we could have done ourselves: waiting in a que for way too long. This was a month ago, and I am still angry about it.

Very well organized day trip! It was worth the long day (about 12 hrs) with a lot of history, beauty and awe packed together in all these three places. Rhys was very knowledgeable, friendly and attentive! Will definitely return to Evan Evans Tours when in London. Rhys and Paul definitely deserve a raise!

I bought two Evan Evans tours for my parents' London visit. On the first one, while they were in Windsor Castle, the tour guide rushed ahead and left my 75 year old parents in the dust. My parents tried frantically to find them only to learn that the bus left without them. Yes, this tour company completely abandoned two senior citizen passengers inside gigantic Windsor Castle, apparently making no effort to find them. Seriously, what kind of tour company does that? They were at least able to put them on a later bus, but that one of course didn't have my dad's jacket and his medicine which were both on the seat of the original bus.

The next day's tour (London) was another screw up. For starters, it was supposed to go to Big Ben but didn't because, as the tour guide put it, "one of the sides of the building is all covered up". So they couldn't go to the other side? My parents (with this being their very first and likely last trip to England) were dependant on this one tour to see England's most famous landmark, and they never got to see it because of this decision on the part of the tour guide. Thanks a lot.

And it gets worse. My parents purposely purchased tickets on this night to see "Witness for the Persecution" because its theater is a 5 minute walk from the tour's dropoff point of Westminster Bridge. One problem- The tour guide decided at the last minute they were going to move the dropout point to Victoria Station, betraying a complete disregard for my parents (and all their guests') itineraries. This ruined their evening. They had to cancel their reservation at Gilray's that was made months ago, forced them to pay for an expensive cab just to get back to where the original drop off point was supposed to be (and where the theater is), and they had to throw down McDonald's for their pre-theater dinner.

This company is careless, irresponsible, and an embarrasment to the tour business.

Was picked up at the Victoria coach station headed to our 1st destination of Windsor castle had to wait more than an 1/2 hour before the gates opened at 9:30. Then had to wait to get into the state apartments which did not open till 10 o'clock. Our time started when we got to the parking lot but it was a 15 minute walk just to get to the gate. Once we got in we had to go through security which was more time so that was over an hour and a a 1/2 of wasted time. Then we were rushed at our 2nd stop of the Roman baths. Once going through their there was no time to go through the town or even eat. After all that on the way home we had to stop at 2 different places to let people off. Instead of dropping everybody off at the same place we were picked up, that was time that had to be fit in which was more wasted time which could have been used at 1 of the tour visits. Then we were not even dropped off at the same place we were picked up at, which might have been good for some but not for everybody. People were quite disappointed that they could not bring hot food or coffee on the bus very disappointing over all. Ryse and the driver Mark S were very pleasant and knowledgeable. So over all the sites were beautiful would have been nice to been picked up later and brought back later to town to avoid the hour and a 1/2 of wasted time at the first stop. Also would have been more courteous to the elderly that can't go through as quickly as the younger people. Maybe there should not have been 3 stops. We all paid good money to be rushed through like cattle.

We booked this tour mainly to go to Stonehenge, but we wanted to see other places too. The tour guide Nigel & driver Tom were both awesome. Learned a lot from this tour. Nigel was so knowledgeable about his country. We did not go to Windsor Castles because it was closed due to the wedding of Harry & Meghan. But we went to Hampton Court Palace instead which I preferred because of its history. Bath was really beautiful. Everyone whose first time to be in this country should go this places in the tour. 👍🏼
Long day but they pack in a lot. This tour hits many of the highlights outside of London. Beautiful ride into the countryside. Plenty of time at each venue. Driver and guide were terrific.

I cannot say enough good things about our tour. Cosette was our guide and Key was our driver. They were just amazing. Cosette was kind but made sure everyone was clear that "the difference between a tourist and a hitch-hiker is about 3 minutes." She was never mean and even made sure everyone was able to sit with their group and that no one changed seats during the trip - added to our comfort for sure. And no one was late at all - I think it was because of how she handled things and was never mean, but was clear about the time each stop.

I think people who are complaining about the time are whiney and should have chosen another trip. It's absolutely ridiculous to think you can have several hours at each stop with 3 stops and so much driving. They knew what they were buying.

So, we had just the right amount of time in each stop if you are like us and just cruise through without listening to every single word spoken through the recorded tour. We had almost 2 hours at Windsor, a little less than 2 at Stonehenge, and a little less than 2 at Bath. We saw the highlights of Windsor (there was no changing of the guard though because of weather), grabbed a sandwich at EAT, saw Stonehenge and the visitor center, and toured the Roman Baths as well as Bath Abbey, plus we visited all the gift shops in each location.

Plan to buy food to eat on the bus. That's just the way it is if you want to see 3 stops in one day. It's a trade-off.

We would choose Evan Evans again.

I knew coming into this would be a jam packed day. But at the end of the day it felt like I spent more time on the bus then at the sites. Overall I spent a total of 12.5 hours on the bus and spending about 2 hours at each stop.

I admit Bath and Stonehenge are not full day stops. At Stonehenge most people are taking pictures then admiring the stones. There is so much history there that I personally could have spent at least 1-2 additional hours to take it all in. But overall the most you need is a half a day and even then that's pushing it. Windsor Castle is the place I wish I could have spent some more time at. The day I went the cathedral was closed so i didn't need to spend the whole day but we only got about 2 hours there but still, with so much to see I was speeding through the exhibits. If I ever get the chance I'd love to spend more time there on my own.

All things considered just know you're basically running against there clock as soon as board the bus. Kevin our tour guide was ok to good. He spent most of his time with us on the bus. At each site you're on your own with an audio device. Which is ok as I like to do things on my own but still. I really noticed it at Windsor where we got there early and there were other for groups there waiting in line for it to open. I saw the group ahead of us and their guide was much livelier and had more energy and was letting everyone engaged. He also made recommendations on what to see first. That to me is the difference between a good guide versus a great one.

The thing that really annoyed me was how anal the bus driver was about "hot" food on the bus. It tour guide recommended we get some sandwiches. So when I was coming back to the bus I ran and got summer McDonald's. A hamburger is a sandwich right? I also got chicken nuggets but yeah not a sandwich. When I got to the bus the driver saw my bag and refused to let me in. He reminded about the no hot food. I thought it was about safety or making a mess. I said my did isn't really hot but he said he hated the smell. WTF. I bet if he didn't see my bag he wouldn't smelled anything. Maybe he had a bad experience with McDonald's or maybe he doesn't like clowns? Regardless it's a long day and they don't build in a lot of time to eat, aside from doing so on the bus. It was a chilly day and I didn't want to spend it eating cold food. So I wolfed down my "hot" food in 5 minutes then boarded the bus. Just a warning I'm not sure if all of the driver's have an issue with "hot" food but I admit I thought about buying a bunch of tuna fish sandwiches or some thing with some blue cheese.

So in summary. It's a long day and you're always in a rush going to and fro. But you do get to see a lot and take some good selfies. Unfortunately what I'll remember the most is an ok tour guide, a long bus ride and don't bring McDonald's onto a bus unless you sneak it in.

Our tour guide Rowan was knowledgeable but a little too much. She is obnoxious and loud and I couldn’t handle her after a couple hours. Don’t even get me started with the bus driver. Lester, the bus driver, drove off the road accidentally, closed the bus doors on a couple with a baby, and forgot to pick us up in Bath. He made us wait 15 minutes in a rainy, windy, 7 degrees! It was not a great experience and we got home later than expected, due to Lester forgetting to pick us up. Why pay so much when Evan Evans tours are this bad? Answer: don’t take this tour

Driver arrived 45 minutes late, in an vehicle that was not adequate. The guide was not a guide, no knowledge, spoke poor english, volunteered nothing, and giggled when asked a question. The trip which was advertised to be 10 to 12 hours was cut short by the driver and we never did get to Bath, Viato/ Trip Advisor was unresponsive.

Very worthwhile tour. Our tour guide was Rhys and he did a wonderful job of giving us the history and insight to start our tours. We had an audio-guided tour (tour with prerecorded bits and headphones) for both Stonehenge and Bath. There was time in bath to eat dinner-- I would recommend "The Pump House" Restaurant at the end of the Roman Baths tour-- fantastic food!

Amazing tour with Mel Adams as the tour guide! He was SUPER professional, kept us on time (extra thanks to Kee, our driver!), and most of all, made the tour fun! Definitely recommend this tour, and if you can get Mell as your tour guide, do it!

This is a one day trip with limited time at each site, Mel (Guide) and Valentine (Driver) made it such that we not only had a good time on the bus but got us to the front of the queue at each venue so that we maximized our time.

Mel is an entertains gentleman who knowledge and take on English history made for entertaining transits and while we waited for Windsor Castle to open he gave us a history of the Tudor era.

The three sites (Windsor / Bath / Stonehenge) were amazing and the time we had at each site was enough (+10-15 to spare) if you keep walking. If you want more time at venues then this tour will be too quick for you and you’ll need to find a 2+ tour to see these sites.

At the end of the tour Mel went and individually check everyone knew how to get from the drop-off point towards their next destination or to a recommended restaurant after a long day touring.

Very timely start at 8am, first in line for Windsor castle which was great! Ate royal ice cream and great pix, back on the coach to Bath. Day ending at Stonehenge with great view and history.

Mel was our guide; funny, knowledgeable and full of great tidbits for food along the way and suggestions for dinner when we ended tour. Our driver was Lawrie. Winning tour and team from Evan Evans !!!

I just finished my tour today and it’s a truly unforgettable day trip. It’s my 2nd time visiting Stonehenge and Bath (which I didnt book any tour last time). It’s a great experience to visit 3 historic tourist spots in a well-scheduled manner, special thanks to our tour guide Rhys Thomas and Dennis the driver. They are very nice and helpful, Rhys provided lots of enriching information (history, spots visiting tips, toilets location, background of the tourist spots) from time to time. Learn a lot from them👍🏻 Highly recommend !
Who would imagine roman architecture and 2000 year old roman swimming pools and hot tubs in England!

With the July crowds this trip resulted in a lot of time spent in the cue (waiting in line) and very little time at the attractions. And let's not forget the multiple (more than ten) reminders "don't be late getting back to the bus, or we will leave you here". I believe it would have been a better experience in an off-peak season but in July is was horrible.

So I took this tour on July 20th, 2019, tour 21, coach 288. Now I don’t usually write reviews but I had time today chal. So tour started off great, first stop Windsor Castle. The que was longer than expected but ok I guess considering the line we met as we were exiting. But here is where things took a turn for the worst for me. I was on the tour with my two kids one of which is only 2 the other is about to be 18, then there was also my sister with her two kids 15 and 20 and my sister’s husband. So first of all you have to be at the Victoria bus station for 7:30am, which was pretty early for us since we drove from an hour away. We had no time for breakfast so we grabbed something quick from the coffee shop inside (which was awesome by the way). First sign that we got off to a rough start they tour guide and bus driver both said no hot drinks on the bus. Ok so throws drinks away because that’s their rule. But when we got on the bus the tour guide was like ok we’ll allow the hot drinks as long as it has a lid on it, smh I already threw mines away. Ok so we proceed to start our day, like I said earlier Windsor Castle was our first stop. We arrived shortly after 8:30am walked over and waited on the que for about 30mins got inside and had about 45mins to walk around the castle before we had to be back on the bus at 10:15am. So of course we had no time to eat anything again but at least we made it on time. Off to the Bath we go 2 plus hours drive so at least we got to rest our eyes. Arrived at the Roman Bath tour guide said our departure time will be 3:20pm so at least we’ll get an opportunity to eat. So we get to the entrance after about 30 mins wait got inside, toured the museum it was great. Now it’s about 2:30 so I’m thinking great I can get something for my kids to eat especially the baby, ordered a pizza and Mac n cheese it was about 3:05 this lady came rushing in the pub where I was waiting on my baby’s Mac n cheese with my daughter saying you guys have everyone waiting on you for 15mins and that is not acceptable, now keep in mind she initially said departure time was at 3:20 and it was about 3:05. So I’m like shocked because I knew I heard the time correctly but it’s not my fault if everyone went back to the bus early. Then she proceeded to say there’s no hot food allowed so you’ll have to throw that out and blahhhhhhhhh now at that moment I had to consider my role as a parent and the fact that I was in the middle of nowhere otherwise I would of left that tour right then and there and open up a disputed with that company. That lady was so inconsiderate, rude and she kept changing the her rules or should I say it only applies to some and our departure time. But the driver was great he was so nice , friendly and an excellent driver, he got us at our destinations ahead of schedule. That lady although you are knowledgeable in what you do you and very rude and need to be considerate of everyone’s need. No one looked annoyed or anything over the fact that we arrived 3:10 oh yeah I guess because they heard her also when she said departure time 3:20 initially. Last but not least when we went to the Stonehenge almost half of the bus came back 15 mins or more late and she said nothing. I guess because I’m black and they were white and Asians she was ok with it right

Very organized tour visiting 3 sites within 11 hours in a day.
The tour guide is good, giving information before visiting each site.

I clicked four stars, then three, then four again, and ultimately landed at three. The reality is that we enjoyed ourselves. We are on vacation and there's isn't a ton you can be unhappy with in this beautiful country, but after reading some of the other reviews, my tour guide didn't measure up. This is a JAM-PACKED day. There's really no room for error or confusion in any direction. You have to get to where you're going, and then stay on track.

Our tour guide seemed a bit overwhelmed and confused a few too many times for my liking. From an operational perspective, I didn't really feel like she was providing clear concise direction on how to get back to our coach, and there weren't too many suggestions on what places we should make sure to see before we hop back on the coach. Considering the amount of time you wait in lines for these - we had to time. Share your knowledge, let me be your Luke Skywalker, I'll take it all in. Instead I was asking strangers where I could find a bunch of busses (yes, coaches, don't worry, he corrected me). I pulled out my voss box earphones to eavesdrop on a different guide telling her people where to find the best deals, and where NOT to shop. Shoutout to her, because it was helpful. Could I have asked, probably, BUT, in a group setting there isn't a lot of one on one time, and since she was relatively confused, I didn't want to add to her stress.

Couple tips - Make sure you bring your umbrella! We had ours, but didn't realize that we would be using it the ENTIRE day, but remember, it's London (adjacent), so the weather is to be expected. Wear layers! You just don't know what's coming, so be ready to bundle up, or pull it off depending on what you get.You'll be able to leave things on the bus if you're too warm (don't you dare leave the umbrella after I already warned you to bring it along). Don't get too excited after waiting in the line for Windsor, look around before you walk in, and grab the audio guide, you'll need it, and at that point you'll be on your own. If you have time, take the walk from Stonehenge back to the Coach (take the shuttle TO Stonehenge, you won't have time to walk both ways). You'll need about 30 minutes to take the walk, but honestly after spending so much time on a bus if I could skip one shuttle ride I just had to. Plan your exit strategy for the Baths. We spent too much time IN the baths, when we only had about an hour and a half, and should have just taken a look and then left to enjoy the city. Lastly, there's no hot food or drinks on the coach. Wasn't a bit deal, but something to keep in mind so you don't buy coffee and then have to chug it in line. You'll have around an hour and a half at each place. It's a VERY tight timeline, which is necessary to see it all, but it's something to consider.

Enjoy yourself, and remember this may be the only time you'll ever be in these places, so the small amount of time you have - use. every. second.

Very busy day, gives you a brief sampling of places and ideas for a future trip. Great value and the quality of Evan Evans buses is impeccable.
James, the tour guide, was condensing and critical of others.

PROS
Andy Jackson - engaging conversationalist and knowledgeable to boot!
Bus driver was skilled at navigating the crooked and narrow streets.

CONS
On our bus (#259), all the left side speakers did not work. In the rear 1/3 of the bus (where i was), only one speaker would work. Made listening a chore!
The weather, cloudy and scattered showers, but it's England!

This was a great day for a solo traveler. It was a jam-packed day at three amazing sites. Each site was beautiful. You have a chance to grab food at each site. The tour guide was amazing--personable and knowledgeable. I highly recommend this tour to anyone interested, from families to solo travelers alike!

It was a marvellous journey to these three atractions. The visity gives us a chance to know a bit. It is a rush trip bit ou Guide "Ildi" and Driver "Lawry" make it easy to stand. I would recommend this trip for anyone who doesn't have plenty of time in London.

We took this tour recently during a 5 day London trip. It lasts about 11 hours, with half the time spent driving in the coach. You spend 1.5-2 hours at each place, with audio commentary through headphones, which is a nice feature. We made a booking for 5 family members, but unfortunately one person got sick at the last minute and could not go. The Evan Evans personnel at Victoria coach station reassured us that we could contact their office afterwards for a refund or credit . However, when we did that, they refused to do either. Most airlines will issue a refund or refund for a medical emergency. However the attitude of Evan Evans was callous and disappointing. Needless to say, we will never travel with them again.

Rhys was wonderful. Its rare that we find a tour guide who speaks clearly, who knows what to say and just as important, knows when to be silent. That said, we would rate the ~12 hr day as very tedious due to the extensive drive times. We are sorry we did not select a less ambitious program!
Windsor is not to be missed and you could spend a full day there. At the opposite extreme is Stonehenge, def not worth the very long bus ride since you cannot get any closer to the stones than ~300+ ft. The Roman Baths were not really worth the trip either just to see a pool of green water, but the town of Bath is delightful.

Suggest you do Windsor and Bath in one day and have enough free time to enjoy Bath. If you have the time, do them separately. Many folks miss the Changing of the Guard at Windsor due to bus schedules so be sure to ask before booking. OTOH, the ceremony is pretty much the same as at Buckingham Palace. See one, see them all.

This is a lot to pack into 1 day, too much in my opinion. You arrive at Windsor Castle before it opens, the queue wraps down the street. You have about an hour and a half to explore, which is not nearly enough time. You also need to squeeze in some time to grab a sandwich to eat on the bus, you will not have time at the next stop, the baths. My seat mate on the bus did not even experience the baths as the line was too long. We chose to spend this hour and a half eating lunch. Finally you get to Stonehenge, wait in line for another bus to take you up to the stones. We arrived back in London around 8pm. Windsor Castle is lovely and Stonehenge is moving, skip the Roman baths.

I found Charlotte, our tour guide, to be friendly, attentive and to know her stuff. Our driver was an expert. The bus was in excellent shape.

We started at 8am and returned at 7pm (approximately). We spent at least 6 hours driving between places.

We got about 1.5 hours to look through Windsor Castle (far, far too little time), 1.25 hours in Bath (see comments below) and about 1.25 hours in Stonehenge (really too much time).

Windsor Castle is huge and rich in history. We could have easily spent 3 to 4 hours in the Castle. It is a must see and do for anyone truly interested in English history. Unfortunately, due to our itinerary for the day, time was very, very limited here. The trip to Windsor took up about an hour on the bus.

We then transited to Bath. The trip was about 2 hours. The bus was comfortable and the ride uneventful. We did not buy the tickets to the museum there. If you don't buy the museum tickets you are pretty much left on your own for the hour plus you are there. We liked Bath, took a walk around the bridge over the Avon river and then found a pub (The Ale House near the bridge). Bath in interesting and the pub was very relaxing (a real British pub). Overall, this stop was a waste of our time - nothing of interest. We could have stayed in London and enjoyed it more.

We hopped back on the bus and spent another 2 hours en route to Stone Henge. Again, the driver was an expert and the transit was smooth and uneventful.

Stonehenge is one of those places you just need to see. It didn't inspire me in any way but, having heard of it all my life, it was nice to put a check nmark by this in my bucket list. Once you get on site, Evan Evans provides you a very nice audio tour using their own equipment (which worked fine). Very interesting to see primitive architecture that is 5,000 years old.

Once done, back on the bus for 2 hours back to London. Again, uneventful.

Our tour guide, provided good history at select locations during our trip. Charlotte is quite knowledgeable.

I think Evan Evans (and any other tour group) would be better off either doing Windsor by itself or perhaps Windsor and either Bath or Stonehenge. The three locations together in one day just wears you out. Spending 6 hours in a bus isn't my idea of a good vacation.

Again, I liked the tour provider but would NOT recommend this particular tour.

Rick G

I will start by saying that I despise tour groups and I approached our tour to Windsor, Bath and Stonehenge with dread.

Thankfully, I found our tour To be the exact opposite due to our guide Phil Bennett. Phil is an exceptionally knowledgeable guide who is able to create a fascinating conversation about British history across a wide range of topics: cultural, linguistic, fashion, etc., without it sounding like a middle school history lesson. Phil also provided our group with insightful information for each sight so that we could make the most of our visit.

As the tour closed and we approached London, Phil spoke with each family on his tour providing recommendations on restaurants, historic pubs, and other urban highlights in London that the average tourist may never experience. Our tour was definitely time and money well-spent, and I recommend anyone looking to visit these sights to book with Evan Evans and ask for Phil.

A special thanks to our driver Nikki is also in order. Nikki cheerfully drove us for almost 12 hours and did a remarkable job maneuvering our bus along those narrow country roads and city streets.

You can also follow Phil on Instagram at tourwithphil

Claudia and Mark or shall I say Sybil and Basil were fantastic tour guides! We thoroughly enjoyed our tour of Windsor Castle, Stonehenge and Bath. It was a jammed packed day but sooooo worth it! This should be a must if you have a whole day to do this.

First and most importantly, our tour guide Emily was amazing! She was extremely friendly and educational and even added a little humor to her stories. She was very apologetic about the days mishaps and gave us GREAT recommendations for breakfast that we asked her for. The Breakfast Club was our favorite breakfast of our entire trip!

Unfortunately, we visited on one of the worst weeks in London - the massive snow storm. When we got on the bus, emily regretfully told us that Windsor Castle was closed and we’d be going to Hampton Palace instead. We were extremely bummed as this was a big reason we booked this tour. Hampton Palace was nice and we were grateful they at least took us somewhere.

When we left Hampton Palace, emily again regretfully told us that Stonehenge was closed due to weather. Now we were extremely bummed! We mainly booked this tour for Windsor and Stonehenge, Bath was just a “bonus”. We didn’t blame Emily or the tour, but we wish we would’ve gotten off the bus at this time.

We took the 2 hour drive to Bath and were able to spend about 2 hours here. We went through the museum in about 40 minutes and ate at a local pub that was delicious! Emily had recommended a bun place.. we didn’t have time to go there so we got one to go and we’re kind of unimpressed with it.

This tour is a lot of time on the bus. We recommend bringing food and snacks. You can’t have hot food or coffee on the bus either.

Exactly as it says, a quick visit to the three sites. Kevin was a great guide and kept it interesting during the bus segments.

Like many other reviews, I agree that you're rushed at Windsor Castle and it's a long drive back at the end. But, there was plenty of time at Stonehenge which is what I wanted. If you have limited time in England and want to see even two of the three places, it's a good way to do it.

Catia was our tour guide, and Barry was our driver. They were fabulous! Tatiana told the stories behind everything we saw and more, but made it very interesting. The weather was so-so, but didn’t matter because we had such a great time. A definite must see! Be prepared for cold, windy, and raining at Stonehenge. I understand it is that way all the time. We did not visit the Roman bad this (our choice), but walked around the village and shopped at a great store named stag, and had the best salad of my life at the pizzeria. I don’t know the name of it, but the owner made the stained-glass panels above the store and inside on the perimeter. Great trip for all.

We had a lovely day around Windsor, Stonehenge and Bath with Godfrey guiding and Paul driving us.
They we absolutely fantastic and made the day very interesting and fun. I totally recommend.!

My husband and I did this tour in on a Friday in December 2019. This is a long day (~12h); we met at 7:00a and got back to Kensington a little after 8:15p, but totally worth it.
I really enjoyed the comfort of the bus tour, the freedom to see the sights on my own time but get recommendations to move around. I found the time adequate for a group tour (Windsor we had about 110 mins, Stonehenge ~90 mins, Bath ~110 mins); please note we were there during X-mas Market, but overall sites were not busy.
We loved Windsor, you actually can easily access Windsor via the train system, so if you're looking to save time/$$, you could do this on your own. Loved the little town, Castle (Queen wasn't home so we got to go upstairs) and the chapel. Our guide was extremely helpful in how to best use our time. Felt like it was more than enough time to move through at a nice, calm walking pace.
Stonehenge, you gotta go, but probably only once. First of all, the wind was unbelievable, borderline sideways and difficult to move forwards. This is at the top of hill, there's no protection from the wind. The walk around Stonehenge was lovely, we kept it brief due to wind and chill. The bus/to from the site ran every 10 mins, so easy to head back (no lines). The museum was quite delightful, very small but you can see often overlooked. We skipped the cafe browsed through a nice but very touristy gift shop. Given no lines, we had more than enough time.
Bath: Absolutely loved the Roman Baths and the town, very cute! The Roman Baths were lovely and a very well-laid out museum, our guide heavily recommended, due to the X-Mas Markets and shops, we only spend about 45 mins in the Baths. We could have easily spent 70 mins, but kept a nice pace of 45 minutes and felt we maximized the experience. Really walked around and enjoyed the live music, X-mas markets and festivities of this adorable town on a Friday in December.
Overall, great value, really enjoyed the guide. Only need to do once, but worth it.

My wife and I took this tour from London and thoroughly enjoyed everything about it. We loved all of the stops, we enjoyed hearing the wonderful commentary from our guide Andy, and my wife even remarked on Derek’s superb driving skills.

I was on this tour on December 1, 2019. I was very disappionted with this tour because it started at 7:00AM until 8:00PM with no breakfast or lunch time imcluded. There was no breakfast to purchase at the train station and lunch had to be purchased and eaten within any of the 40 min tours. We was told we can not eat or drink on the bus. Each tour was 40 min long . We was unable to complete the oral tour at the sites because they was longer thasn the 40 min allotted. We had not eaten for thre whole day. Customers are on the bus traveling longer than the time allotted to see the sites. I hope this is helpful to future ciustomers considering taking this tour because the hotel personnal was not familiar with these details.

This is a very quick day trip from London, although you will be able to see all that you’d like to see. The tour guide Jennifer and Driver Kee were great. We were not prepared with how lovely we would find Windsor and Bath... Stonehenge was just “ok”.

As I was exiting from the rear door of the bus at Windsor Castle, the automatic door began to close on me, then the bus started driving away. As a result, I fell on the pavement, sustaining a serious head injury. The tour guide had left the area, and the bus driver came to see me after being alerted by other passengers to stop the bus. After the ambulance and the police attended the scene, and I was treated for the wound to my head and made a police report, I continued on the bus trip, but was not able to walk very far, so could not visit Stonehenge. I have not received an apology, the offer of a refund or any other consideration, and I have not been contacted by the tour company to inquire as to my well-being. I believe that tour guides should ensure that all passengers are safely off the bus before leaving the area, and that the bus drivers should make sure their passengers are safely off the bus before driving away.

You guys are absolutely great! Guide (Leslie) was very acknowledgable, always willing to answer on every question. Driver was vary flexible with extra stops if needed.
On that trip they use alternative rute though countryside to show you this beatiful area instead of boring motorway!
Just book it!

My tour was amazing!
Chris had such great knowledge and brought the tour to life, loved every minute.

Jennie O

We had a delightful, full day visiting three wonderful and historical locations. Our tour guide Katie was bubbly, cheerful, knowledgeable and conversant in a wide range of topics. Valentine was our driver, deftly threading our comfortable coach through a wide range of roads, including narrow and twisting ones.
Despite having a November forecast of rain, the only downpour was during the drive from Windsor to Stonehenge. Katie’s extensive experience (and Cambridge education) helped us know exactly what to expect at each stop.
Our only challenge was finding Victoria Coach Station at the beginning of the day. Hint: it is a bit of a walk southwest of Victoria Station (the Underground Station). Driving back to London was after dark, which was fine.

Well done Nicholas( it think) and our driver valentine. Very informative full of knowledge and felt safe the whole time.
My only downside was my husband and l didn’t sit together because they crammed the bus and people don’t like to sit next to one another and ended up with a couple always talking over them😜
We were the first in line to the castle so that was a great start. Very windy and cold so was glad we didn’t have to wait long and got in first. The castle is beautiful and got to see lots and wasn’t to crowded for us, which I was glad.
Next stop Stonehenge. Wasn’t what I expected at all. However our guide was once again informative and made sure we didn’t wait and told us times etc to be back on bus etc etc. took photos of us, and nothing seemed to much.
Until you have been here it really doesn’t set in what you are looking at and how it got there.
Bath was a beautiful place and as everyone has stated could have spent more time. Still enough time here to see as much as u can cramp in.
The journey home of course is a pain but that’s what u get with a 12 hour tour
Would recommend to everyone.

Although a long trip, about 12 hours, our guide, Mel was very funny and informative and added a unique perspective to the trip. Mel kept our group moving in order to maximize our time at the various stops, instead of wasting our time standing in line at the attractions, as there are many bus groups that were also touring this route, although we never felt rushed. Mel kept us laughing with his stories and fascinating details of Windsor Castle, Bath and Stonehenge. This is a great day trip our of London and was one of the highlights of our trip!

Tom, the guide, was very knowledgeable and hospitable—he walked around to all 51 passengers at the end to ensure they knew which tube station would get them to their destination. Kee was an excellent driver who got us all over the countryside safely! Thank you both for an amazing experience!

Tour was fantastic. Our tour guide, Mel was the absolute best and made our trip so entertaining. The bus rides were long, but Mel made them entertaining and even checked on every single person to see if they knew where they were going after the bus got back.

Mel was a knowledgable and entertaining tour guide. It was the longest tour as is was in the countryside of England but Mel kept us informed and entertained. I highly recommend this tour to everyone! :)
It was very organized and safe. Our tour guide was very optimistic, kind and extrovert. Our driver did excellent by taking us everywhere on time. Mel and Michael thank you.

Mel Adams and our driver Michael hosted a great tour to Windsor Castle, Bath and Stonehenge on Oct 9. Mel was extremely informative on the history of all the sites and very engaging. Michael did an excellent job with the driving. I would recommend, without qualification, taking this tour especially with Mel and Michael. Marc and Robin

Evan Evans your was just perfect! Our guide Mel (driver Valentine) we’re perfect & kept us on track all day! Loved hearing the history & stories on our way to each location. Anyone looking for this tour it is a must! 3 locations & beautiful sites on the way.

This is a very nice tour if you want to get to know 3 amazing locations in one day.
In victoria coach station the staff from evan evans was very helpful and it was easy to find were to go. Our guide was Omar and the driver was Jane and they were both very nice, lots of history facts were told and was a very safe drive. Because the locations are quite far from each other, you spent a lot of time in the bus, but that is expected, as well as a tight time limit in each place. We spent about 1h45m in windsor castle and got to see the apartments and the chapel; 1h30 in bath, including the tour of the roman baths (it's better without the audioguide otherwise you won't get time to see it all); 45min in stonehenge. Bring your own food so you can save time (and money) in each location. Totally recomended!

Had a wonderful tour with Mel and Kee! They made sure to hustle and keep the group on time. We were the first in que for the windsor Castle! Mel, provided great history lessons, had a great personality and was very entertaining. Kee drove like a boss, a safe boss!

It was the best trip!
No issues at all,
Mel was the best! He guided us thru all 3 places and answer every question we had

Our first stop was Windsor Castle. We were given just under 2 hrs here however that time was decreased because there was a changing of the guard and in order to get to our bus on time and get a bite to eat before boarding, we had only about an hour. Our audio equipment also failed and we had to get it exchanged. The audio tour itself it also a bit confusing. Further, since we were pressed for time, we weren’t able to listen to it all. That all said, the Castle is stunning and really impressive. Realizing that the Queen and royals before her actually live/lived there makes it so relatable.

Our second stop was Bath. What a spectacular city! The charm will capture your heart even as you approach and steal it forevermore once you’re there. Our tour was only for the Roman Baths but again it too felt rushed. Barely left enough time for a snack or bathroom break. The baths themselves were very interesting but I couldn’t help wishing I could just tour Bath. This will definitely be a place I come back to for a few days.

Our final stop was Stonehenge. The most pleasantly surprising stop. We weren’t originally too interested in seeing this as others had said it was boring. We however found it fascinating. It was truly a beautiful day and the stones were very impressive in the late afternoon setting sun. The audio tour was very informative and leaves you with pondering just what these stones were amongst other questions. Perfect amount of time allotted here. Wasn’t too busy either which made the experience even better.

Our guide Manon and driver Steve were great. Manon was witty and informative. Steve a very capable driver.

So I’m left debating whether to recommend this tour. Had I known more about the current format, I would not have done it. However I’d never have learned about the city of Bath(which I plan to return to). I’d suggest Evans and Evans look at alternatives to allow more time at each spot or at least make it clearer how much time is permitted att each stop. There may be other tours more suitable for what we were after but assumed they were all similar. Do your homework before going to be sure of what your getting. This may just be your cup of tea.

This is a fantastic trip! With Eugene & Austin as great companions, we had a superb day trip to these locations smoothly!
