Was a really great tour and our guide Patricia was great as well as a driver Marc. The bus ridge was nice and the locations were amazing, wish we had more time to see the to explore the town of Bath. Also wish we had started in Bath so we didn't have an almost 3 hour ride home at end our tour.

It’s an early start and late finish, however this tour packs a lot in and that’s what you sign up for - 3 sites in a day! Godfrey and Tom were excellent hosts. Godfrey kept us informed and amused. He kept us to time, and really respected that we had paid money for the tour and ensured we were not held up by people that were tardy with time. We did leave 2 stops with 2 people not turning up on time, and while they were lucky to get a ride on another bus, Godfrey handled it very well and didn’t make the other 35+ people who were on time, wait. Tom was an excellent driver, navigating busy traffic conditions and we felt safe at all times. Thanks for an enjoyable day. The hosts always make the difference. Highly recommend this tour to anyone thinking about it.

The 11 hour tour of Windsor Castle, Bath, and Stonehenge was comfortable, thanks to our bus driver, Tom, and extremely interesing. Our tour guide, Rhys Thomas, was well informed, courteous, and very entertaining. I highly recommend the tour.
It was a long tour but we knew it when we signed up. Mel, the tour guide and Steve, the driver made the trip fun and helped us focus on seeing the high points of the stops efficiently.

Mel was great, made the tour a whole lot of fun. He kept us informed and educated us on a lot
of history about each stop as well as London. We would definitely recommend this tour and especially Mel as a guide. We can’t wait to come back again!!

We were so fortunate to have Alexandria for our tour guide and Abbey as our driver for the day. Alexandria's knowledge of overall history as well as each location on the tour was VERY extensive. She was very clear on instructions for departure times and suggestions to see as much as we could during our time at each location. I would only suggest to tell guests traveling to Windsor on a Sunday, that the chapel has services and you might not get to go inside. If you are able to request Alexandria, you will not be disappointed!!!!

We had a great time in this tour of Windsor Castle, Bath and Stonehenge! Our tour operator, Evan Evans is organized and the bus is clean and comfortable. We exceptionally liked our tour guide, Andy Jackson who is very informative and engaging (Thank you also to Joe who drove us safely). We learned so much of England’s history because of Andy! The only comment we have is that since this is three places in one day, time in each is short and may feel a bit rushed. Otherwise, this tour is Highly recommended!

This tour crams 3 wonderful sites into 1 tour and doesn't give you enough time at either of the first 2 (Windsor or Bath). If you want to see 3 sites for the first time and get in a couple of pictures, then this tour will meet those goals, but otherwise, it is too rushed. You get 45 minutes at Windsor, not nearly enough for the grounds, State Rooms, and St. George; then 1.5 hours in Bath, which includes lunch, so not enough time to read and learn anything about either site. Our tour guide told an off-color joke and blabbed on forever about Henry VIII the entire day - not sure the relevance- overall, the weakest tour we took on our vacation in the UK.

Took the tour yesterday. Great way to get a little taste of each location! We had approx 1 hour at each location. We took the underground to the Victoria underground station and followed very well posted signs for about a 5-7 Minute walk to Victoria coach station where the buses leave.

** highly advise to get to Victoria coach station early**

As soon as the bus is full they load them and send them giving you a head start! We were there and got in line around gate 1 around 7:30. They pass out wrist bands and stand in line along the gate. WiFi on the bus 👍🏻 very comfortable and semi reclining seats! Norma was and excellent guide. Very knowledgeable and takes the time to answer questions to enhance the experience and make it easier to navigate back to the bus. Tom was our very skilled driver!

Would of liked a bit more time at Windsor castle, but you have to move on to make it to all locations! We were the first in line to get into Windsor castle at 9:30 ( they let the groups in a little early), but the state rooms where not open until 10. You have to wait in another line outside the building until then. Had enough time to just walk through the state rooms and St. George’s chapel. We grabbed lunch and ate it quick before getting on the bus for Bath. There is food available at each stop. The only question is if you’ll have time to grab any. We packed sandwiches so we didn’t miss out on any of the attractions. Roman baths were very historical and fun. It was a nice quaint town. Le Crêperie has delicious ice cream and crepes close to the pick up spot. Stonehenge was fun to see! They have a visitor center for food, merch, and restrooms! You take a bus to get to/from the Stonehenge spot!

They make two stops on the way home. One near the hotel district then also at Victoria coach station as well!

Book this tour is you are short on time and want a little taste of each site!

This tour was the highlight of my trip. We had James as our tour guide and he was phenomenal. If I could take him as a tour guide wherever I went in my life I would.

He was so knowledgeable and funny. We definitely hit the jackpot with him as our tour guide as he is also a historian. He took the time to answer any questions we had about England, or anything for that matter!

If you want to a see a little of everything this tour is for you!

Our guide, Andy Jackson, is the best!!! I booked this tour via Klook.com and my husband and I are very lucky to have him as our guide. He made the whole day tour very fun and interesting. Aside from being funny, he shared a lot of useful information about the places we went to and passed by. It was a day well spent!

We all meet the Evans Evans tour at Vitoria Coach station we boarded the bus and met the Tour Guide Cartia and Bus driver Mow she made sure we left the terminal on time and explained that we all needed to be punctual as their is a lot to see and kilometres to travel in one day that suited us as we have little time in London we need to see as much as we can. We really enjoyed the whole trip a little hectic but you can expect that. Cartia explains everything the history and dates she a fantastic guide. At the days end she was starting to loosing her voice also very helpful with all passengers she didn’t miss a thing we enjoyed the whole experience and Mow was the perfect driver. We did three tours with Evans Evans their Drivers were excellent in the city and on the highway we felt as safe as houses with them. The other two guides were well experienced and knowledgeable as well. Our tour agent in Australia had us pay all tips before we left so we didn’t have to worry about tipping. I hope that the Evans Evans Guides and Drivers get there’s as they did a Professional Job
Regards
Barry

I highly recommend purchasing this tour!! Arrive at Victoria Train station. When you enter, you’ll see a sign that says “Evans Evans Tours”. This particular package comes with entry to all locations which is super convenient. You’re separated into different tor buses that have a tour guide. I sincerely hope you get Mel, absolutely AMAZING tour guide/historian. The bus provides free WiFi. The only con to this trip is you’re covering a lot in a short amount of time. So you don’t get to stay at each location for more than 2 hours each. But again, it’s an incredibly worthwhile trip!

The tour we took included an extremely knowledgeable tour guide who offended two of us by calling us “antiques” in an effort to get us to agree to senior tickets for the castle and Bath attractions. Very annoying! The tour was very long (about 12 hours) and we did get to see all three places, but we only had 1 to 1.5 hours in each place, so not nearly enough time to enjoy ourselves. We were told at Windor Castle that we weren’t allowed to bring bags or carry anything, which was not true—it was just a way for the tour guide to try to get us through security more quickly. Please note that the tour guide only gives you information on the bus and right outside each attraction—you go through the attractions on your own, using an audio guide. I expected the tour guide to accompany us, so that was not good.

I never write any reviews but for our guide, Phil, I cannot stress how EXTRAORDINARY he was on our tour. His knowledge expands across the UK and even outside. A whole bunch of relevant and random knowledge. Seems like Phil is a walking Wikipedia and was eager to learn from everyone. Phil was able to keep everyone engage, enthusiastic and alive throughout this LONG trip. He even gave a group of 51 people one on one time and recommended places to eat, drink, hangout or converse with. He genuinely loves his job and cares for his tourists. I seen other tour groups from a different company: bored, no headset, and not enjoying their time. Glad I booked here.
Spectacular Job on Phil’s part.

As far as the trip goes, there are a couple of things to note.
- The guides announce they WILL LEAVE you if you are late for any of the 3 events. Tourists from other coaches were seen left behind but our guide waited about 10 minutes(which is more than what other guides did and were left behind).
- Bring water and snacks.
- Headphones for music. (1.5-2 hours drive to each destination and return trip as well) but as I said before, not necessary with our guide Phil.

Windsor
We started off going to Windsor, which is phenomenal. Your tour guide will not escort you around but you have reasonably time to do everything if you walk at a fast pace. You can spend a full day at Windsor with a train that lands within walking distance. There are also many shops around so keep an eye for on your time.

Baths
Amazing town. Shops. Food. Souvenirs. Etc. Rather than going into the Roman bath tour, we’d rather explore what the city had to offer. Had amazing Fudge, shops and food around. You can also buy the tickets to bath (which is like a 5-10 min tour).

Stonehenge
As you seen on TV is how you see it in real life. Full of mysteries but rich in history. The closest you can get is maybe 30 feet away, but the backdrop of open skies and lands makes this place much more. Bucket list checked.

Very important about this stop:
Shuttles takes you from your coach to site but at any given moment, you can be in line with 300 people ahead of you. As I said before, your tour guide wishes not to leave you so don’t push it. We were running past the gift shops to reach our coach. We got in line 20 minutes onsite for our shuttle and arrived 5 minutes AFTER departure time. Give yourself 30-45 if you want to browse in the Gift Shop and want to go back.

We took the tour yesterday with Evan Evans and it was a Day well spent. The bus left on time, Mark the driver made our journey very smooth & James our guide was extremely helpful, courteous & funny. The places we visited were rich in history, beautiful to look at & overall simply amazing. Certainly a wonderful time was had by all & would recommend this tour & the company to anyone exploring the same.

We did the Stonehenge, Windsor castle, and bath tour from London. Our guide was incredible, I can't remember his name but he was very knowledgeable and had worked as an archaeologist at Stonehenge in 2005.
The sites were very busy as we did come in peak season and he was very understandable and changed the departing times so we could see every place properly.
He even came with us down to Stonehenge and gave us a full history of it where as other drivers tend to just stay behind.
Unfortunately on the way back to the coaches my partner and I got stuck in a rather long line. Our coach was supposed to depart at 6pm and we could see it as our transfer bus pulled up but by the time we got to the car park at 5.55pm it was gone. Thankfully there was another Evan Evans bus still there and they took us back to London - lesson learnt, don't be late back to your coach or they will literally leave you behind! Thanks you for an incredible day though!

Excellent tour with Claudia and Steve. Bus was comfortable and Claudia was very knowledgeable and witty. Early arrival to Windsor made the queue short giving us time to tour the castle. Enjoyed touring Bath, plenty of shops and places to eat. Stonehenge was awe inspiring . Very easy to reserve on TripAdvisor and got a great deal last minute. Highly recommend!

My friend and I really enjoyed our tour with Windsor Castle, Bath and Stonehenge! We wanted to see all of these places but also didn't want to spent a lot of days outside of the actual city of London on our stay so this tour was perfect to see everything in one day. We also planned our own stay/itineraries for the rest of our time in London so it was great to have a day where everything was already planned out for us and we could just relax about planning anything.

You get around 1.5/2 hours I'd say in each place which I thought was perfect for us. We had Godfrey as our guide and he was great- he was organized and very knowledgeable about the sites. I highly recommend this tour!

I recently moved to London and having a friend come to visit I figured it would be the perfect opportunity for us both to see a bit more of what’s on offer. Kee did a great job manoeuvring the coach, and James definitely made the tour with his knowledge on everything (there wasn’t a question he couldn’t answer), his quick and dry wit, and his willingness to look after us no matter what. We were some of the first into Windsor Castle which was a bonus as the only downfall was the lack of time to properly see it all. It was a highlights tour though, and it definitely makes me want to go back and visit again! Bath was absolutely beautiful too. Definitely recommend this tour.
Very disappointing. If you want to see Windsor castle, DO NOT take this tour. You barely have time to walk through it

We started at Windsor Castle and enjoyed our self guided tour. The place is beautiful and the staff is very helpful. We then drove to bath and enjoyed an old Roman City. We toured and had a pint in a local pub. We then drove to Lacock and had lunch in a pub built in 1350. This is where I got my fish and chips. Then on to Stonehenge. When you come up over the hill and there it is, it is quite an experience. Lucy and Steve were wonderful tour guides and bus driver. This tour is well worth the money and time.

We were out for a full day. Went to the Victoria coach station to take the tour bus. Our tour guide was Godfrey (I think that was his name). He was knowledgeable and gave us bits and pieces of info of the places that we visited.

First off, we headed to the Windsor castle. The castle was still closed when we reached, but there was already a long queue formed outside the castle. Once the castle was opened, it was rather fast moving. We were free to roam around ourselves in the castle. Personally I would prefer a guided tour.

Then we proceeded to Bath to see the Roman baths. The untreated water was greenish in color. We were told that we could get a taste of the clean water but we missed it as we couldn’t find it. As there was still time before we were due to leave, we walked around the town. There were quite a lot of shops and eateries. As it was during the World Cup, there was a free screening at the open area.

Lastly, we went to Stonehenge. This was the place I was waiting for. The stones and formations were really spectacular. Lucky there was a shuttle bus from the visitor center to the stones as the weather was very hot.

We were back in London before the sun sets (in the summer). The trip was well timed and the guide was great.

If you enjoy hoards of people descending on a historic site and ignoring the keep off the ancient artifacts signs this is your place to be! The interpretive center is quite good but the hoards of people taking selfies is disgusting and not respecting the site is beyond belief. The drone of a highway adjacent to the site is very distracting and there are far better sites elsewhere in southern England that provide an authentic experience without the crowds and the kitsch. This visit was a disappointment...and I would not go out of my way to make the visit. A lot of hype with not much going for it unless you can get a private showing.

Due to my tight schedule I decided to chose this focus tour to the 3 location. Stonehenge I was not expecting much as I am aware of what to expect. However, still disappointed that no guided tour in Windsor or Bath only Audio guide (May be it is the policy of the 3 location).

The tour guide was very helpful when I lost my phone. She is very knowledgeable.

From a personal view point but I believe if the tour details show audio guide I will have selected something else. On second thoughts, maybe all UK tour are on audio guide.

Wanted to give a four as the tour was on time and cover all the highlight area. However, my personal preference of guide on the premises change it to 3.

Our guide, James, was terrific. He’s a historian and had so much knowledge not only on the stops we visited, but also on the towns and surrounding sites we passed. He was super informative and it was educational while fun, as he has a fun sense of humor. James with excellent driver Steve, made the long day a wonderful adventure.

Chris (guide) and Kai (driver) were great. Chris is full of corny jokes, but he really does know his stuff. My qualm is not with the guide or the driver, but with the extreme rushed nature of this tour.
We arrived at Victoria's station at 7:30 as advised, and waited for an HOUR before we left on the bus. I know London is famous for its love of queuing to do anything, but it seemed disorganized as a whole. First stop was Windsor Castle, which had a "short" queue of 30 mins. We only had 50 minutes in the castle, which was not enough. We saw St. George's Chapel and State Rooms, but didn't have time for the Doll's House. When we ran back to the bus, we were told after we were rolling away our next stop wasn't for 2.5 hours in Bath. That's too long without a stop without informing people beforehand.

I'm the most disappointed with the lack of time in Bath. We literally had 50 minutes to queue, see the Roman baths, and eat lunch. It's not worth seeing the Roman baths when you have 10 minutes to do so. Don't pay for the tour of the Baths, you won't have time to see them fully. I love history, but I also needed to eat. Having to chose between food and a tour was not fair. Part of this issue I observed was we were always waiting to get group tickets. On other tours I've been on, the tour guide already as the group tickets. I don't know if that's possible, but it could save precious time. The morning delay of an hour clearly ate into our afternoon tour time, which was extremely frustrating. Chris recommended the Cornish pasties for lunch, which were amazing. They're a hot pocket type thing filled with meat, veggies, and cheese. Delicious!

Two hours later, we arrived at Stonehenge. This is the only stop of the three where I felt we had a decent amount of time. It's worth it to see, it really is fascinating.

I've been all over Europe, and I realize we traveled 280 miles in one day. I know lines are a thing at places like this. I highly suggest starting earlier or ending later to really get what you paid for on this trip. I've been on tours that start at 6:45 and end at 20:45, and while yes, they're long, you get what you pay for. Start on time, change the order, or reduce the attractions.

Catia was an excellent guide and gave us a lot of British history. Trip provided a very quick overview of three sites. Great if you want to fit a lot into a single day. Must grab quick foods along the way as there isn’t time to stop to eat.

Went on this trip with my mom. The guide Rys, was extremely personable and knowledgeable and worked really hard to explain a lot of the tours attractions. The bus left on time and was clean (but had no bathroom on board, although all the visiting places had bathrooms). We got to Windsor Castle before the gates opened and were one of the first groups there. There was definitely enough time to browse Windsor Castle if you followed Rys' suggestion of going to the state room first. The tour to Bath was scenic, there's only really enough time to browse the Roman Baths, so if you want to walk around the streets of Bath you should plan to stay there a day. Finally we arrived at Stonehenge, for which there was enough time to go up and look at the stones.

Overall a great trip and a great guide. Would recommend Evans Evans tours to everybody who wants to see these three main sites in one day.

Chris was one of the best tour guides that we have ever experienced, and we have toured a lot. He made the trip informative, funny, and he planned the trip so we were not waiting long in any lines at attractions. Beautiful trip!

The tour was very impressive! Exceeded my expectations. Bosco, who was our driver for the day was great, and Chris. the tour guide was full of very interesting facts and hilarious jokes throughout the tour. Each place we visited was amazing, and we had just enough time to do everything we wanted at each stop.
Stonehenge was made very interesting, as Chris has studied archeology, and so was able to explain the significance of the stones and the history, which was an added bonus!
A wonderful day overall and would definitely go again

Overall we enjoyed the destinations, but the amount of queuing at Victoria Coach Station and Windsor did not seem a great use of time. Windsor in particular had long queues that used up at least 90 minutes of our time, and it seems we could have avoided some of those lines if we had simply left the station on time.

Our guide was knowledgeable and enjoyable overall. He added interesting commentary at Windsor, Bath, and Stonehenge. The microphone system was very helpful for listening as you didn't need to huddle near him whenever he spoke.

In all I'm glad we went on the trip, but I feel like a smaller group that left on time in the morning would have probably left us feeling less rushed and herded around like livestock.

We took the day tour from London to Windsor Castle, Bath and Stonehenge. Our guide, Godfrey was great! He was very informative and was very nice. Our driver, Michelangelo was also great at his job! Hitting all three sites in one day, we did feel a little rushed through certain places, but in all we are truly happy that we got to see all we did. If all tours through Evan Evans Tours were like the experience we had, I would highly recommend this company. Stonehenge is a must to see as well as Windsor Castle!

We had a tour of Windsor Castle, Bath, and the Stonehenge with Oliver, the tour guide, and Bosko, the bus driver. They were awesome. Oliver told us about all the best spots, restaurants, and shops, and he was informative at each of our stops! Busko was a very smooth and safe driver! Even with rain and narrow roads, he made it look easy! My family quite enjoyed the tour and will use Oliver and Evan Evans tours should we end up in London again! Highly recommend!

Read the reviews in TA and booked this tour on 23 May. We could easily locate the bus terminal in the Victoria coach station and the check in was quite easy.
The staff - Alan our guide (gentleman with the hat and pipe in the photo) and Bob our driver were very courteous, nice and knowledgeable. Alan's commentary was very interesting and add a tinge of humour. Thanks for that.

The time given at each location was enough and with all tickets already purchased the queuing up was less infact we were the first ones to enter the windsor castle.

One thing is that you have no time for lunch hence get something packed... This was already informed at the beginning.

Overall a nice trip and we enjoyed it.

We had a great day doing this tour, our guides were Katia and Joe, lovely people; however, just not enough time in Windsor Castle. We got to see Windsor upon opening, but only got to see the cathedral before it was time to leave. Stonehenge was ok, can’t get very close to the stones, so I almost wish I skipped Stonehenge for more time at Windsor. Bath was ok, but if you aren’t very interested to see it I’d try another site. Booked through 360 Tours, almost missed the bus because we didn’t realize Victoria Coach station is different than Victoria (tube) station.

We thought it might be too much in one day, but it didn’t feel too cramped or rushed. Great day, great way to see these amazing places without the stress of trying to navigate yourself. Kudos to Oliver, who made it easy and fun for us today! And Graham the driver - both wonderful!

This was our first time in London and this tour was one of our Highlights. Left London at 8am and returned at 7pm. Katia was our guide and she was well informed and very helpful. Also the most attractive guide I've ever had.😍 Dave, our driver and world traveler was an excellent driver. My only complaint was that Windsor castle wasn't open when we arrived and we wasted a lot of time waiting for it to open.

Tour guide was very knowledgeable in the history of each place we visited. Great tour. I would recommend this to anyone.

They could better communicate with you on where to catch the bus. I arrived early as directed, but the desk doesn't open early to answer questions.

The tour was great. Our guide, although not British but from Brazil, was very knowledgeable. The lines were going everywhere. Line after line.

Our first stop was Windsor Castle. We skipped the doll house as there was more of a line. Keep a fairly fast pace as you only get about an hour at the castle after waiting on line for security and to get your tickets. Go through the state apartments and then you may catch the changing of the guard. Off you watch the whole pro session you will miss something else at the castle like the state apartments or the chapel.

At bathe, I would go straight to the bath and then go to the museum. It is VERY crowded and you can barely see what anything is, hear your audio tour ( which is inckuded), or enjoy it at all. I would honestly recommend seeing the bath and then strolling the streets of the town and getting lunch. You are only in town about an hour.

Stonehenge is magnificent. It was quite windy and chilly so I would bring a sweater, scarf or something just invade outside of summer months. You must again wait in line to get on a bus to take you to the stones. You can walk but on this tour you will not have time. You do get a free audio tour for the stonex. This is handed out in the bus before you get yherr. I would recommend listening before you arrive so you are aware of what you are looking at and then a!so do not waste time. Tour the museum after. You may need to do this quite quick as again you only have an hour there and with the wait for the bus to and from it eats up quite a bit of time.

Bring snacks for the bus. Nothing not to eat or Fri at any point on the bus. We honestly had no time to get any food while we were on the tour so it was good we had our snacks.

It was definitely worth the trip out of London!

This is a good tour if you want to see all of these sights but not delve deeply into any one spot. Too much time on the bus compared to time to explore but it’s understandable considering the distance travelled. It may be better to see these places individually.

I took this tour with Oliver on March 13. This was a great trip for a sampling outside of London. Oliver was personable and kept things lively without overdoing it. At the end of the trip he even spoke with each of us on the best way to get to our hotels and food suggestions near the station.
I am staying near Westminster and it was an easy 20 min. walk to Victoria Coach Station. I was pretty exhausted at the end of the tour so took a black cab back for about 8 pounds.
You do spend as much time riding in the bus as you do at the stops, but the bus is comfortable and with limited wifi.
You don't have quite enough time at Windsor, 30 min more would have been great and the castle staff doesn't let you take pictures inside the castle or church which is a bummer.
Stonehenge is something to say you've seen but at the end of the day not very exciting, especially since your view includes 200 other people there with you. You spend as much time in the line to shuttle out to the stones as you do snapping photos and coming back. Evans tours provides a voice recording of the site that is informative.
I was more excited about seeing the two above but at the end Bath was much more exciting. The Roman baths were ok but the town itself asks to be explored. We got there in the afternoon and unfortunately some sites were already closing. Would have loved more time here to see churches, parks, museums and had dinner. This warrants it's own trip.
A very long day, at station by 8:40 am and back around 8:15 pm, but a nice tour. Might recommend two stops with a longer stay at each.

My boyfriend and I had a great time today. Best part is we didn't have to worry about transportation and our tour guide Kevin was awesome! He made the time go by fast. Would definitely recommend this tour! Just be on time when the tour guide gives you specific time to be back on the bus. Would definitely use this tour company again with any other upcoming tours!
Hardly believable how much we were able to see in one day. Rhys and Thom were perfect team. Rhys is really funny and knowledgeable guide. This day was really great.

It's tough to believe how much were were able to see in one day, but it all happened rather seamlessly. I was a bit nervous because I read some reviews that said the tour packed too much into one day. But, while we were watching the time constantly so we wouldn't miss the bus departure, I felt like we had spent enough time at each location. I wasn't particularly interested in seeing Bath, but wow, it's such a fascinating and beautiful place, I'm so glad it was part of the tour! That ended up being my 11 year old's favorite as well. They actually even have an activity book there that engages the kids with questions about the exhibits, which my son had fun completing. The bus ride was smooth and the driver drove very safely.

Be prepared for a very long day, but it is completely worth it! Our guide, David, was very knowledgeable and full if information that he enjoyed sharing with us. He made the trip fun and we loved learning little hidden things about our destinations from him.
A lot of people told me not to waste my time to go to this attraction, but I disagree. I went with my 3 kids on this trip and they were in awe. I thought it was pretty cool!

First off, the tour does exactly what it says, so no complaint there. However, it IS very rushed, especially for the first two places we visited (Windsor Castle, then Bath). We basically needed to run through the tour in Bath without stopping to listen to anything on the audio guide. We did have a good amount of time though at the last stop (Stonehenge) so for us that was the most enjoyable part of the day trip.

Our guide Nigel was pretty good and experienced. We and another couple joined the French tour, which turned out to be a part of the English group. So there were a few of us at the front of the bus, with all the rest in English. Since Nigel needed to say everything twice in two languages, I guess inevitably it did get a little bit repetitive for those who can understand both languages. But of course that wasn't anybody's fault.

All in all, the day trip was quite enjoyable, but if you can afford the time, I would recommend covering only two places instead of three in a day trip because you would really feel like you're being rushed everywhere.

Me and my boyfriend booked a tour in the uk through Viator for a day trip to Stonehenge, bath and Hampton court of the 14/08/17. We paid $317.42 which included a lunch at Stonehenge and early access to Hampton court. We were really excited about this as we really wanted to visit Hampton court which was why we booked this tour. About 2-3 days befor the tour was to start we received a ph call to say that unfortunately the tour we booked was cancelled for Hampton court but we could change to go to Windsor castle instead. I asked if there was another tour we could do that included Hampton court but there was not even though on their website it stated otherwise. We were offered the Windsor castle package or our money back and because we still wanted to visit the 2 other sites we reluctantly agreed we later found out that lunch was not provided on this tour which angered us even more as this was another reason why we booked the tour and so we had very little time for a decent lunch at any of the sites. As a result we are extreamely disappointed with the service from this company and would not recommend them to anyone nor would we book through them ever again.

This was a great way to get a quick look at some of the most popular attractions near London. The tour was well organized with a dynamic and interesting guide (Dolly) who kept us on our toes. We learned all kinds of information about the visited sites, the royals, English history, and volumes of trivia (some of which should be taken with a grain of salt ;] ) Lunch was a simple but satisfying boxed affair which kept us on time as we are it in transit. There was a lot to see so don't expect to look in detail at any one location. Windsor castle was incredible, Bath picturesque and historic, Stonehenge inspiring.

Notes for travellers:

1. There are no toilets at the bus terminal (unless you buy something at a small cafe) so plan to use the facilities elsewhere before arriving for the tour. There is a toilet on the bus but individual drivers may keep it locked (This varies by driver; ours was locked). There are public toilets at Windsor castle, bath and Stonehenge.
2. Be on time; don't get left behind

First, you have to have the right guide and driver. Graham, you are a master of your craft. You and Lazlo made it a very enjoyable day. Restored Windsor Castle is stunning. You can only imagine the stiff collars and pretentious dinner conversations in the Great Hall. Changing of the Guard was impressive. Stonehenge is a head scratcher in the middle nowhere and around a lot of crop circles. Me thinks the ETs like the English countryside. How can you not especially when its sunny. Final stop Bath. Have a pint or two before the long ride home.

The tour was very rushed.. Like VERY.. we are young adults and a teen, pretty fit and we had to run to see everything... In Windsor we spent about 40 mins in the queue and then rushed through st George's Chapel... Hubby wanted to go through Windsor Castle as well, but there was literally no time since the main gate was being closed down at 11 for the guard change... We managed to run through Windsor rooms in just 6 mins and then headed down to the exit gate... Managed to get to the coach at 1130am. At Stonehenge we opted to walk to the stones and took the shuttle back. We spent about 10 mins at the stones and didn't manage to see the exhibitions at the info center. In Bath, if you want to see the Roman spas, you have no time to explore the village which is not big, btw and not much to see, anyways. I wish we could have spent more time at Windsor and maybe skip Bath which was the least interesting for us. Our guide, Andrew, though, was exceptionally good! He S never stopped talking since we had left London and was entertaining and fun. Thanks to him, the tour was a pleasure and not just a rush

Manon was our guide and she was great, informative and funny…
I liked the fact we hit three places and they were long enough to see everything I wanted…

Guide - Lesli was extremely informative, polite and helpful. She was very professional and explained everything…I.e. days plan, instructions on meeting points etc. very clearly and was very acessable, she would even walk around the bus to make sure she answered all our questions before getting to the destination. She was very knowledgeable about the locations and history. She even went out of her way to tell us about what was around Victoria station for dinner and suggestions when the tour ended and we are being dropped off.

Driver - I’m sorry I didn’t catch his name clearly, I believe it was Barhad? My apologies to you if I got your name wrong…anyway, he was very nice and went out of his way to help us. He drove very safe and yet was right on time, or at least their planned scedule.

Bus - Mercedes bus, extremely clean looked brand new. There was a sink and toilet but no one had to use it, I think it would have been for an emergency.

Price - Great value…I mean what else can I say besides it’s well worth the money and we had a great time! We left a 20% tip at the end of the tour and it was our pleasure to do so.

Mel was a fantastic guide full of knowledge about English history. Oxford is slightly overwhelming around this time of the year (tons of people, and all of them in a hurry), but overall the tour was a great way to hit several spots in one day.

This tour was nothing as advertised nor was it something that I have experienced in past tours of the sort. I emailed the tour company and asked what time we would get back from the tour- they replied to me while I was on the tour at 13:00… this was not helpful. To start the actual day off- the bussing situation, I am 5 feet 11 inches tall and my father is 6 foot 4 inches. The entire ride around was a painful process and left us cramped and hurting in more ways than one. Not only this but the tour says the bus includes WiFi- when asking the bus driver Jordan about the WiFi he said it does not work. Well great… also we were told to use the provided seat belt- mentioning that I am very tall I also have huge breasts. I am a DDD and the seatbelt would not buckle across my chest- this was not even an average belt it was ridiculous. I went on this tour with my 2 elderly parents- one of whom was the very tall gentleman. As soon as we got to Windsor castle our guide rushed up and basically ran to get in line. My parents were having problems keeping up and this is not a tour that I would suggest for elderly couples. Not only this but we had less than an hour to explore the entire premises including the chapel. It makes things even more complicated because we had to be to the bus at 11:30 or it would leave without us- this was made clear and in fact some people were left behind. During the changing of the guards ceremony the door was locked and we could not leave and had to plan around this leaving even less time to view the castle! Now where was our guide during this time to tell us some history or help us through this? Well no where- we were told to meet at the coach though I saw other guides stuck with their groups who worked with Evan Evan’s. Now onto Stonehenge- same situation, our guide gave herself the time to use the bathroom as for the rest of us it was go go go. It was essentially a photo opportunity and we did in fact leave people behind who did not make it back, probably because our guide was not with us. Our guide only showed us a clock with the time to be back and would not say what time to be back for whatever reason. Now thank God I can read a standard clock but I felt bad if others couldn’t see or didn’t know how to read a clock.
The baths were the first time things weren’t terribly rushed so that was probably the only enjoyable part of a painfully long day. I would not recommend anyone book with this group. I understand these are 3 sites in 1 day but I rather start earlier and stay later or just have a better approach and attitude about the whole situation. It really spoiled things for my entire trip.

If you are short on time, definitely take this tour! Used Global (there are others) tours and was glad. Tour departed very early resulting in us being the 2nd group to line up for entry to Windsor. (Group line DOES get VERY, VERY long the later you arrive.)

Opt for ST George Chapel "FIRST" if seeing the Queen's resting place is high on your list. Going to the Apartment first might result in you NOT GETTING INTO St George because of the "queue" length and running out of time before needing to get back on the bus.

Stonehedge - rest area is immediately adjacent to tour bus drop. Get to the shuttle (short path) ASAP to max time circling the Stones. DO NOT GO TO THE FOOD/GIFT area first! This mistake ( I made it) will cause extra uphill walking and wasted time. But, the site itself is well worth it!

Bath (Roman Baths) provide a great step back in time to neat architecture. Upon leaving bus, note the area BEHIND you toward the hills. Tour probably leads into the town ahead...but the RIVER and GREAT picture spots are in the HILL direction. If you forget this, there might not be sufficient time before re-boarding the bus to view the river, Neat narrow streets and shops and architecture neat. BATHS and history are well documented.

SInce this is the last tour stop, time might be crunched depending on folk's discipline on returning to the bus ON-TIME at prior stops! Global drop off is at tube Gloucester. A quick walk from here following Google maps to ROCCA, an italian eatery ( we ate here 4 thumbs up) puts you across the street from the South Kensington tube stop ...and back to central London.

If time is on your side...consider a separate trip trip via rail to Windsor. Train ENDS at the station exactly where the tour buses drop off passengers. Castle entry for individuals is adjacent to Group entry portal. Individual travel will allow more time to explorer the State Apartment and probably more fully enjoy the audio tour. There IS A LOT OF HISTORY!

The same with BATH! Train is relatively close ...a little over 2 hrs back to London (vs almost 3 via bus to the Gloucester stop).
The tour was fast but informative and we got to see 3 places in one day, driving around 300 miles. Could have used more time at the castle, it was a bit of a rush

This trip was amazing. Our guide (Mel) was the best and I could go on a trip with him again and again! I would like to give him 6 or 7 stars, but this is imposible so here goes 5 stars! Greetings from BaRbaRa and we wish you a good live!
Fantastic tour! Highly recommended. Was very impressed with the quality of this tour and how knowledgeable our tour guide Godfrey is. The experience was enriching and that of a lifetime.

Wonderful experience, I learned so much from the tour guide Catia. She was amazing!!! She was able to asswear any question I had for her and made the whole tour very enjoyable and was a great learning experience.

This started out as a good trip but in Bath we got lost and tried calling Evan evans to help ask the tour guide if it was possible to meet up with us at a familiar store to help lead us back to the bus.

The operator at evans evans not only just said we can’t contact the tour guide but every response was extremely unhelpful which can be summarized as, I am sorry but that’s your problem and it’s not our fault (no one was blaming you, I was asking for help). And then they cut my phone call.

Your possible responses to my above situation would most probably be:
We will wait additional time for late stragglers but we can’t stay at the parking spot as it would be unfair to other passengers and our tight schedule. (This is unhelpful if the customers are new to London and what more a place which they were dropped for less than 2 hours, but please refer to my win win suggestion below).
Follow other people. (It is not easily done as everyone have their own plans and may not be heading towards the bus immediately. I would not want to be considered a creep.)
Memorize the routes: (like I said there are genuine stragglers. This is even worse for people whose English is not the first language and may be able to understand but unable to ask for directions quickly enough from strangers).

My suggestion: instead of having your tour guide just waiting at the bus, how about taking the extra mile and either give a number for a phone just for tour guides during tours only (this is so private number of tour guides can be protected) so any lost customer can contact your guides in advance OR wait at A focal point near the place we are touring instead of just going straight to the bus and say meet me there. This way anyone not familiar may still be able to find the focal point nearby and get on the bus on time so everyone wins.

Your tour guides were funny and insightful but why not go an extra mile and also prepare for contingencies for people who genuinely got lost?

Are the operators and people working in the Evan Evan so rigid that at 5pm sharp they knock off by putting the phone to voice mail despite a customer distress call or the procedures for leaving a place so strict and gives no room for slight compassion for genuine stragglers? I have read through the reviews and know I am not the only one with this challenge.

Your final response might be: other operators also act like us.

Even if that is true, do you not want to stand out and be different to attract the market?
I have heard about other operators (whose names I can’t disclose due to confidentiality) who actually have agents who actually cared to find stragglers or give a focal point if anyone got lost that is near the site they are touring.

I will not name the tour guide I was with this time due to me believing they were under strict orders on how much they can help and I do not want to hurt their source of income. This is me showing compassion even though I am very disappointed.

I will however be sharing my honest reviews with the many travel companies back home.

I saw that you often ask to contact customers to discuss how they feel if they are dissatisfied but I still see there are many with the same issues as what I just faced so unless the above is remedied, I do not think we have anything to talk about as I wrote in detail on what you can do to be better.
Our guide Mel and driver Merrick (? Spelling? ) were fabulous! Mel is well educated, smart, informative and charming. I highly recommend this tour.
I had a really good time at this tour with Mel and John. Mel is a really good and personable guide with tons of knowledge and a quirky personality. You won’t regret this tour!

DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY. We have now taken this tour twice. Once in 2016 & once in July of 2022. The first time, everything went fine, so when we were heading back to London with a group of eight in July, we thought we'd try again. Let me start by saying that as travel professionals who have been on countless excursions all over the world, my husband & I can honestly say that this company's complete lack of customer service is some of the worst we have experienced anywhere. Read on for the complete saga.

First, we originally booked in two groups of four because we were splitting the cost & could not do multiple payments on the same reservation. We didn't think this was going to be a problem since we booked exactly the same tour on exactly the same da at exactly the same time.

However, when we arrived to check-in on the morning of, we were told we were on separate coaches because we had two reservations. We asked the woman checking us in, her supervisor & our tour guide, Simon, if there was anyway we could go on the same coach since our group had been split up and we got the same answer every time: No. But it won't matter since all the buses go to all the same places at the same time. We trusted this information & reluctantly got on separate buses.

The information we were given proved to be completely untrue. We all started at Windsor, but half our group was a full 30-minutes behind the other. We had to nearly run through the state apartments & St. George's Chapel so that we could see and do them together as a family. Half our group then had to be back on their bus sooner than the other and it wasn't until we had pulled away from Windsor that we figured out that half our group was actually now headed to Bath first while the other half was headed to Stonehenge first.

We asked our tour guide Simon about it & he told us there was nothing he could do, which we understood since we were already on our way. However, when he said we would have to call customer service & we asked for the number, he didn't even have it & said we would have to look it up on the website ourselves. So, we did and when we called they told us if we had brought it up that morning, they could have fixed it at the station. Our complaint is that we DID bring it up in the morning right at check-in & three different people refused to help us get on the same bus & all three then proceeded to give us bad information that everything would be fine & we would get to do everything together except ride on the bus. The customer service agent on the phone then pushed off our concerns & instead gave us an email address to send our complaint to.

So, now instead of simply enjoying our tour as a family as we intended, we spent our time on the bus writing an email to their customer service team to see how they were going to make it right while half our family is going in the complete opposite direction of the other half. To say we were frustrated and thoroughly unimpressed with the customer service we received on the day of our tour would be an understatement. But then they continued to prove their unwillingness to help us afterwards.

After a week or more, we did receive an email back from their customer service team in response to our complaint & request that they make it right, which more or less blamed us for everything. They told us it was our own fault we got split up & that it was our responsibility to find other guests on the other bus to switch with us. This is completely ridiculous. Since one bus was meeting to leave Windsor 15 minutes before the other was leaving, there simply wasn’t time to hunt down other guides or other guests & ask them to switch with us. How were we supposed to meet up as a family, see the site & connect with two tour guides & negotiate with other guests to get ourselves on another bus? This really is a ridiculous notion. Their staff should have rearranged us when we asked them to before we ever left the station. It wouldn't have been hard at all to switch a group of four for a group of four. It would have been so easy & simple, but no.

We responded to their email that blamed us for everything & again, asked them to make it right. It has now been several weeks & they have conveniently ignored that email. Thus, here we are leaving an honest, but poor review in the hope that they recognize how terrible of a job they did handling this situation & hopefully to encourage other people to use a different tour company other than Evan Evans.

Horrible service. We booked for a tour on 7/22 during the rail strike and didn’t know that the train service didn’t operate until 8am on that day just because 7/21 was the rail strike day. So at 6:30am in the morning, we all knew about it (we stayed next to the train station and saw people waiting and talking) and then called Uber to get to the pick up location. Unfortunately all the Uber rides got cancelled immediately. So we called the operator and asked for help. But no help at all. At first, she said that no cancellation no refund etc. and the. She told us to go to the pick up location to talk to a team member. We asked if can go directly to Windsor castle to meet the tour there but no response. So we went to the pick up location later when the bus already left and the team member told us to catch a train to Windsor castle to meet the tour there, but no guarantee that they would pick us up since we still have to call the operator again and the operator would call the driver and arrange the pick up. We’re so upset about how they operated. We’re tourists and this was our 1st time in the UK but they just tried to make us go without helping anything. And surprisingly I couldn’t find the customer service for Viator or TripAdvisor to contact. Expedia provided much better service I think. When I couldn’t check in my hotel due to a snow storm and road closures, I called Expedia and they helped to talk with the hotel and got refund for that night immediately. I would rate 0 if it let me.
This trip was great, we got to see three of the best destinations in England and out guide Robert was great, super funny and informative.
We enjoyed all the information and the history of Stonehenge and Windsor Castle. Godfrey was very humorous and Corey made the trip fun.

Well, our experience with Evan Evans was a short one. As a group of two, we signed up for the Windsor-Stonehenge-Bath tour. We were taken to Windsor, which due to the central London traffic took about two hours. Meanwhile, we were regaled with our guide's ad hoc and gaffe-prone commentary (no, I don't think that Prussia is currently Austria, not at all).

Arriving at the castle at around 10 am, we were led from the parking lot, through the train station to the castle, where we were told to walk the castle tour by ourselves and watch the change of guards. After the change of guards, we should meet at Queen Victoria's statue in front of the castle at 11:10. We were also told that the gate will be closed during the change of guards, but that is ok, as it will be opened immediately after.

As the recommended time at the castle by the tour is 2-3 hours, we walked through the state apartments at a brisk walking pace, skipping St. George's chapel and the gift shop. Arriving back at the gate, the change of guards was happening. As soon as this finished, we walked to Queen Victoria's statue.

To make the story short, they left us there, taking our bags that were left on the bus. After waiting for about an hour and frantically going back and forth between the meeting point and the parking lot, we tried to call the company, who told us that they left, and we should try to pick up our luggage the next day, which we did. With subsequent communication, they have told us that in their view they don't owe us any refund.

So now, with this experience, let me try to make a plus and cons list for this tour and company.

Pros:
+ The bus is nice.
+ Everybody at the office was polite, and they did return our bags.

Cons:
- The schedule, I assume adjusted for the traffic in London, did not make it possible to visit Windsor castle in any meaningful way. Forget about the St. George chapel listed in the tour: we skipped it, and they still left us in the street.
- The role of the guide appears to be to talk on the bus - she did not come with us to the Windsor tour. You are left to deal with the audio guide provided by the entrance. We are guessing that this would have also been the case at Stonehenge and Bath.
- There was no means of communication with the guide. There were no backup plans. The meeting point was far away from the bus, so if you end up waiting at the meeting point, the bus will leave without you and you will never notice.
- The company does not seem to care about leaving customers at the stops. There was no attempt to contact us - they relied on us contacting them - in our case, through international phone calls. They are cheerfully and politely blaming us for missing the rendez-vous. It seems to be a regular occurrence.

Suggestions to travelers:
* Understand that what you are paying for is transportation, and discounted tickets to the attractions. This might be worth it, but please don't assume that this is one of those tours where the tour guide is walking with you and presenting a personal perspective of the sights.
* Please make backup plans, and ensure that you have some idea of how to return to base, if the company leaves you on the street at one of the stops, as it did for us. This was relatively easy for us, with two trains from Windsor to Slough and then Slough to London Paddington. Make plans ahead from all the stops.

I highly recommend this tour if you are comfortable with “speed dating” tourism. Going to Windsor, Bath, and Stonehenge in one day is a lot. Only Evan Evans Tours could do this the right way. Extremely professional, detailed, and attentive.

Simon, our tour guide, is extraordinary. Fascinating knowledge of everything everywhere we went and thoroughly professional. Ollie, our driver, is a pro and extremely friendly.

IMHO, Stonehenge is the only place you can see within an hour and feel like you’ve taken it all in. Windsor and Bath probably deserve an entire day, apiece, but this tour will provide you focus on the highlights and leave you feeling satisfied…that you saw and appreciated the most significant aspects of Bath and Windsor.

Highly recommend unless you are one of those people who likes to stop and stare at every single exhibit in a museum!

Thanks Evan Evans and Simon.
Really enjoyed this tour. Our tour guide, Eugene, was the right amount of funny and is very entertaining. Highly recommended!!!

We had a great time on this tour. Reese was very knowledgeable and provided interesting commentary throughout the trip. Luan was our driver and delivered us safely to our stops. Glad we chose this company for our tour!

Great way to easily see 3 wonderful sites. Our guide Bruce was not only extremely informative but funny as well. He was very helpful making sure we didn't get lost and kept us on time. The tour felt a little rushed at Windsor but you have to realize the tour is taking you to 3 key sites that are an hour or so apart from each other so time must be efficient. You will walk fast and it could be a little difficult if you have limited mobility although not impossible. Also either take a lunch or be prepared to buy one (most likely at Windsor) to eat on the bus.

As a side note we booked this tour after another one through Viator was cancelled without telling us.

Mel was an amazing guide and our bus driver was great! Wonderful experience- highly recommend! Learned a ton and saw a ton. Always wish we had more time but I know what I signed up for! Definitely the most cost efficient way to see all 3 things

Was a very big jam packed day. Had a great time. Saw alot and ticked many things off the bucket list all at once. So handy.
Our tour guide Rowan was exceptionally lovely. She was very knowledgeable. Pulled out some fun facts, cracked jokes and also knew about each place as if she were a local.
Thank you.
This was an awesome tour. We were guided by Bruce and driven around by Amrish. Bruce was congenial and very informative. Overall this was a must do tour and I highly recommend it
Efficient way to get first impressions all within a day. Mel (guide) is knowledgeable with a great sense of humour. A thoroughly enjoyable day out of London.

Nicholas was amazing! He shared so much great insight!

He knew all the tricks and ensured our trip was awesome!!! Our first stop was Windsor Castle- and I felt like our group was the only one there- it was delightful. Then we were off to Stonehenge it was breath taking- he had so much historical knowledge- I’m so glad he was our guide. Then we were off to the Baths- he put us in front and ensured we were taken care of it, and pointed out some great eating spots. My daughter and I had the most wonderful day, these memories will last a life time. Thank you so much Nicholas! And a shout out to Jose our driver, smooth drive and we were on time to everything- thank you!!

I first want to say that this tour company is very professional. We had some challenges with being in the UK during the crazy COVID high Christmas holidays, and it really impacted everything we did, including this tour (not their fault, on our end). We did have to reschedule and I felt that they were accommodating and willing to help us (although, a reminder to check the refund policy when you purchase).
My only feedback to the company is a reminder that many of us, being on holiday, are like... scrambling. It would be a little thing, but SO NICE, if you had coffee or tea or juice or all of that in the office while we are waiting. The tour leaves early and we have to get to the office, so to be welcomed by some warm beverages would be a nice thing.
The tour is good! It is QUICK but my husband and I really felt that it was enough time to see everything. It feels FAST (especially Windsor - felt very fast) but honestly we never didn't miss anything lol. So, it is totally fine! They just don't like cooked smelly foods on the bus so take some snacks that are easy on the group. Food does feel rushed except maybe in Bath where we didn't go into the bath so had lots of time to walk and get a drink, but we managed (aka I gulped my coffee while walking to the bus - not ideal but there you have it).
Take warm clothes for everything - Bath is all outdoors and with COVID even eating outside etc. but layers are good for the bus. There is a little storage above your seat where you can put things to be more comfortable. I DID inquire about storing our luggage and they don't do that, and a big bag won't fit on the bus.
Our driver was excellent and the guide was informative - it is a long day! Hoping they make decent money and we tipped, of course.
You will get a little ear thing microphone for stuff which you will use very little, honestly. Some people didn't have tickets to certain things so be sure your tickets include all the sights if you want to see everything.
The tour guide, Nicholas, was very knowledgeable and kept the group engaged. Beautiful sites and covered so much ground in one day! A lot of time on the bus but was worth it

We purchased an Evan Evans one day couch tour of Windsor, Stonehenge, and Bath during our recent December 2021 trip to London. Our guide Mel and our driver Joe were both wonderful. Mel provided us with extra historical tidbits while traveling on the coach and walking to each site. He also handled all the details for our entry to Windsor and Stonehenge. Joe, who was also our driver for an early trip to WB London Harry Potter studio tour, provided us with a safe and relaxing drive to our destinations and then back to London.

Quick tip: confirm location with Evan Evans of coach pickup. We were picked up right outside the Evan Evans office. I think during busier times pick up is at Victoria Coach Station. They sent us an email confirming the pickup location the night before our tour.

Windsor: Be advised. Due to time constraints from it being a 3 stop day trip, security to get inside a castle still used by the Queen, and Covid - we only had 40 minutes to explore Windsor Castle. Windsor is a complex with multiple buildings. Once through security you can pick up a map and audio guide and then do a self guided tour. We knew we wanted to see St. George’s Chapel where Harry and Megan were married. We took our time visiting the chapel, which is stunning and filled with history, then poked our head in the gift shop. We then started our walk back to the coach. The walk back is maybe 10 minutiae. There are lots of food and shopping options on your walk back.

Stonehenge: you park away from the site and take a shuttle bus to it. Evan Evans provides an audio guide and map that work together. While walking around Stonehenge you can stop, touch the map with your audio device to receive commentary. You cannot walking into the center on Stonehenge, but you can get pretty close. Plenty of time here to leisurely walk around Stonehenge, visit the gift job, and get a bite to eat at the cafe. Also, they have bathrooms.

Bath: Full disclosure, we’d planned to see Oxford, but that trip canceled and we switched to one that included Bath. I guess this your only allows for a smaller subset to visit the Roman baths in Bath, England. So if you really want to see them, book early, and confirm with the tour company. We had just planned to do some shopping in Bath. We walked to a Christmas magnet which had local artists, then started our way back to the coach, stopping in little shops on our way back. I’d recommend doing some planing on what ti do/see in Bath to help make the most of your time.

Return to London: fair warning - from Bath back to London is a 3 hour trip. So plan accordingly. Bring a book, headphones, or a pillow. Cold drinks and cold food are allowed on the coach, but no hot drinks or hot food.

Summary: if you are staying in London, this day trip is a great way to get outside the city and see three great sites, while leaving the details and driving to Evan Evans Tours.

Loved it!
Mel and Joe were fantastic, Mel especially was knowledgeable as well as very personable.
If you get a choice at all in your guide, ask for Mel and you will be guaranteed a wonderful tour.
11/10, would recommend again and again.

We booked this tour through Viator. Our tour guide, Carol, and our bus driver were both amazing, no issues there. The bus was comfortable, but it did not have anywhere to charge your phone.

The main issue with the tour was that it was too much for one day. It's about 300 miles round trip. We arrived into Windsor around 9, but the castle did not open until 10am. We had to be back at the bus by 1115. The changing of the guard was at 11, which means you needed to be out before that. In the end we had 45 minutes to look around. Not enough time. From there we went to Stonehenge, which was fine, plenty of time. Then we stopped at the Red Lion in Lacock for a pub lunch. After that was Bath, where we has a little over an hour.

If I did it again, I would book Windsor and Bath, and do Stonehenge on another day. Don't rush it! There is way too much to see. I only gave it three stars because they packed way too much into the day and you didn't have time to enjoy anything.

But it was cool and we had a good time. Bring money to tips the driver and guide.

3 Canadians on a last-minute business/pleasure trip to London. This is one of the only things we didn't get to do our first time here, so we had to check it off this time round. Joe was our driver, and our guide was Reese. What a guy. He is witty and extremely knowledgeable. You can tell he's passionate about his role, or at least extremely comfortable, as he can drop any random tidbit of knowledge on something otherwise possibly unassuming, and in a well timed manner. He was very upfront about what to expect. It is a lot to pack in to one day, but it is doable, so there it is. He guided us on what to sort of expect at each stop, given our schedule. Which was immensely helpful. Of course, this means you'll just want to make each of these places their own day trips in the future. Windsor is stunning, plus the Queen was home! Stonehenge was off season so less busy and the city of Bath. I am telling you now, you will be happy for your experience, but even a full day is hardly enough time to take in the beauty of this UNESCO site. As it was November, Reese was also donating gratuities at the end of his day with us (for the month) toward men's health, and that's pretty awesome! Good guy. Big heart. As for covid, we didn't feel unsafe at all. Coming from Canada where as of now, our rules are more strict, they were clear and informative about everything up front. We all kept our masks on on the coach, and as required in any location. Everything was clean. He communicated about eating, how long we have, where washrooms were. We felt very taken care of all day. Great job Reese, great job EvanEvans.
The only thing I'd have changed about our day under the circumstances, if at all, was the uncomfortably loud fellow at the back of the bus near us. Not hugely loud, but Reese did include the fact that people pay good money for these tours and we deserve to enjoy them, and nap as needed etc (it's an 11 hour tour). The guy didn't hear...or something, so he got a lot of dirty looks and woke up many people, including myself and companions - but was absolutely oblivious to his constant chatter to the poor unassuming girl beside him. Haha. Not EvanEvans fault. And not even a real true issue, but hey. Giving the bad with the good. If you're strapped for time, or a way to get out of town, this is a great option. You won't regret it :)
We did the tour to Windsor Castle, Stonehenge and Bath… quite a task for one day but really rewarding… expertly guided by Leslie and chauffeured by Paul! Thanks for the pleasant trip!

Nick and Dennis, thanks so much for such an extraordinary tour experience...i indeed enjoyed every bit of it. The windsor castle is out of this world.

We had a lovely day out at the stones. It was a lovely stop off on our way to Cornwall. You can see for miles. Highly recommend.

Mel was a wonderful tour guide! He was very knowledgeable, witty and just an overall gem of a tour guide! Paul was great, too! The tour was really good. Enjoyed all 3 place, guide Richard is really nice. HE Gave us all the useful information about the place.....

You get to visit 3 marvellous spots in just one day, timing is perfect and you can check some interesting places.Richard and Larry were always so kind and entertaining, they helped us and gave us tons of info. Totally recommend!
We thoroughly enjoyed our day with Eugene and Dave touring Windsor Castle, Stone Henge and Bath. 10/10 would recommend.

My son, best friend and I thoroughly enjoyed the trip! Godfrey was a very knowledgeable your guide and Barry made sure that we got to our destinations efficiently.

Funny guides, friendly team who are synchronized and helped us get on board the right tour when we joined late.

Absolutely wonderful, would recommend them to friends.

We were in London for a week and debated going out to Stonehenge for a day trip given there’s SO much in the city to do and explore, especially for a first time visit. We found Evan Evans tours online while doing some research of Stonehenge trips, specifically regarding access into the inner circle and site itself. Evan Evans was the most affordable to offer the inner circle that we found and it’s a must do—don’t bother going to the monument without going up to the stones before anyone else arrives for the day. Groups typically have around 50, but ours was only 12, so it felt really special and exclusive. We had Stonehenge essentially to ourselves for about 1.5 hours, with cooperating weather in the early morning.

The trips to Oxford and Windsor were nice, but too short—at least a nice introduction to a glimpse of these cities too was fun. Need like a half day at each, but made sense to do them for 1.5 hours each given the driving and overall itinerary. Nice 30-50 min walks with an expert guide explaining the history and locations and sites at each.

The guide is critical. We were fortunate to have Andy Jackson who served in the British military and police for decades and brought a wealth of expertise to these sites. He certainly was passionate about these places and well versed.

The bus and driving (Joe) was top quality as well. Very new and comfortable during the road travel.

Highly recommended.

Jennifer and our driver Ashton did a great job! We got everywhere early enough we didn’t have to wait in long lines. The day is worry free if you pay a little more and purchase the trip with passes included!
My sister and I had a wonderful time! Highly recommend!

Sacha and Elisa were our driver and tour guide. Elisa was an excellent driver and Sacha was a vibrant and energetic guide who was extremely knowledgeable about the history of the area. We had a wonderful time.

Nice was to see key sights in England in one day. We could have used a little additional time at Windsor Castle. Tour guide Kevin was awesome.

Highly recommend this for any explorer looking to get a lot done in one day!
I took my mom on this tour and we loved it!!! We were able to see Stonehenge, Bath, and Windsor castle all within the same day!! Godfrey and Paul were great!! Would definitely do it again!

I am NOT a tour and bus guy and I only review Restaurants on Yelp. But I had to resurect my TripAdvisor account to post this review.

Paul, our driver most artfully thread this beast of a bus through the bus terminal, London, Slough, Windsor and Bath like he was driving Mini Cooper!! I can't stand anybody else driving me, but felt safe all day, and even took a snooze. There are not enough stars for me to say that compliment any better then that. My wife gets very car sick and she was fine by a window and in the middle of the bus, which she was worried about. The seat are not too high and you can see all around.

Godfrey our Guide, well I would love a full keyboard and my laptop, but my little pos pda samsung will cause me to be pithy and sharp.

My personal favorite desintations on this tour would have to be Windsor castle, follwed by Bath and last Stonehenge. Which really surprised me. Last tip, Bring some cold food with you if you want to eat on the way. There is plenty of opportunities to buy food at the destinations but most of the time, you don't have time because you are so busy taking pictures. The reason the food has to be cold is because you can easily smell food on the bus when you are traveling so it becomes and issue. I didn't bring food but I ate McDonalds before we boarded the bus in the morning and bought some amazing cornish pastereries which we ate as we explored the town.

Went to London to see the traditional sights and enjoyed it all!. Loved seeing the palace, the Castle and the Tower Bridge. It was all very interesting and we will be BACK! We even took the Tube to our Hotel because the traffic can be too much and the TUBE is comfortable and very reasonable! We want to go next to the museums and the Winston Churchill War rooms next. The people were very nice and helpful. We enjoyed the English Pubs and of course the Fish and Chips! We went in May and it was wonderful weather. Have fun!

Our tour guide gave us so much detail and background we would have never known otherwise if we had gone on our own. Great tour with an especially terrific guide (Robert) and driver (Michael). Easy, efficient, and affordable.

Love that I get to see 3 important places to see outside of the city.

Reputable, experienced and professional operator - one can instantly tell by their fleet of red Mercedes buses at the coach station, as well as the fact that the tour director (Richard) and driver (Collin) both wore ties. Godfrey is a qualified and dedicated tour guide.
He’s very knowledgeable about the history of the places we visit.
Alton is a careful, skillful and polite driver. He’s very friendly too.

I had great tour with Evan Evans, especially with Godfrey as guide and Alton as driver. The tour was arranged well and on-time. Godfrey gave some hints about the destination and he informed any unique/important places we passed during the tour. The coach was also very convenient.

A very entertaining full day, led by Mr Godfrey and the bus driven Mr Alton. Mr Godfrey is very well versed with his knowledge and ibformatiom give loke a peefect tour guide.

We had a lovely time, visiting incredible places, knowing a bit more of history; our guide Paty and Paul, the driver, were absolutely brilliant. Thanks a lot, very worth to try.

Excellent tour. Both guide and driver were very professional, and guide was extremely knowledgeable as he attended university at Oxford. Never a dull moment.

GREAT tour - sites were amazing - Kevin was an excellent guide and our driver was very professional and safe - this was our top experience on our trip to London - wished we had more time at each stop, but then would not have been able to make it to all 3!

Peter was and excellent expeditor. Was an amazing journey many thanks for a driver also.

My family and I had such an incredible time visiting Stonehenge, Windsor Castle, and Bath during the last week of November. He was very approachable, charismatic, and witty—we really learned a lot from him and wasn't surprised to find out that he's also a scholar and author! Our day tour started and ended punctually, and was both very organized and enjoyable. We were lucky to have the sun come out during our Stonehenge visit! Highly recommend Evan Evans Tours.

My husband and I have nothing but good things to say about this tour! Definitely one of the highlights of our trip in London! Antonio was a great driver, especially with the Sunday crowd out and about. Vaughn's natural humor and knowledge of the sites definitely made the tour worthwhile and he went the extra mile by making sure we made it home at the end of the day. 10/10 for us.

Nice photo display of visitors past in the indoor museum
Excellant representation of tools and clothing hands-on area in the thatch covered reproductions. Interesting to chat with the docent about life during the period.

Evan Evans Tours did a nice job planning and executing the day trip to Stonehenge, Windsor Castle and Bath. The departure from Victoria Station was orderly and on time, and George made sure that the coach was comfortable, secure and professionally driven.

The day started at Windsor where we arrived a little early so we had to wait a bit outside before being permitted to enter. This was offset though once inside because we dealt with so few other tourists who had not yet entered. Depending on the weather and time available, you may be able to plan to see the changing of the guard but be sure to leave enough time to return to the coach on time for the departure to Stonehenge.

Although the ancient rocks alone are the main attraction at this next site, be sure to take your time and observe from each of the different viewpoints around the entire formation. The awe of this point of interest is in its simplicity and complexities. It's humbling and reassuring of just how intelligent our ancestors were so many thousands of years before our current day tech.

The time at Bath was the perfect close to the full day. Sit back at one of the benches around the water and enjoy the beautiful architecture, civil design and various sculptures.

On the whole, the day was long, but broken up into easy-to-manage segments. For sure it is intended to be a day trip that delivers an overview of these sites and offer the advantage of not having to drive to each one of them separately. Also, Peter was very informative, good-humored and considerate.

It was a good tour if you want to see many things in one day. We got a taste of each of the sights. It was really rushed and you can only see a few things in detail

The main problem for us was that in Windsor castle, the gate was locked at 1045 am and we were meant to be back at the coach by 1115. Our tour guide told us if the gates locked we would be stuck inside for 45 mins but that the gates locked at 1055.

I called Evans tours to let then know but the person on the phone told me the coach left, even though I called at 1050 and the coach was not meant to leave until 11:15. This caused me a lot of stress and I felt that the person on the line did not care.

We managed get out from Windsor castle and get to the coach at 11:15 but the misinformation caused a lot of stress. It put a huge damper on the rest of the trip.

Over all, I would probably not do such a tour again.
